jobs.title: HRIS Analyst - Senior (Workday Advanced Compensation)
jobs.excerpt: #WeAreONEOK – Fortune 500 company.  100+ years in business.
jobs.description:
#WeAreONEOK – Fortune 500 company. 100+ years in business. Leading midstream service provider. Safety first. Sustainable operations. Environmentally responsible. Employee focused.

JOB SUMMARY

This position is eligible for remote work in one of the following states: Arkansas, Colorado, Georgia, Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Louisiana, Minnesota, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas, Wisconsin, or Wyoming. This position will require some travel for office meetings, as needed, to our corporate office in Tulsa, OK.

The Opportunity 

We’re looking for an experienced Workday professional who sees HR technology as more than a system to maintain. This is a consultative, solution-oriented role for someone who is curious about the business, thinks ahead, and proactively brings ideas for how Workday can better support our people, HR teams, and organization. 

The ideal candidate combines strong hands-on Workday expertise with eagerness to listen, challenge assumptions, evaluate options, and turn business needs into thoughtful solutions. You will work closely with HR Centers of Excellence (COEs), HR Business Partners (HRBPs), HRIT, and other partners to understand what they are trying to accomplish and help determine the best path forward. 

We are looking for someone who can bridge Workday leading practices with the realities of our business. That means bringing expertise and a point of view while remaining flexible, approaching challenges with a “how can we solve this?” mindset, and recognizing that the best solution is developed in partnership with the people who use it. 

This role will have a primary focus on Workday Advanced Compensation module, while supporting broader Workday capabilities as business needs evolve. You should be comfortable moving between strategy and execution: advising stakeholders, identifying opportunities, recommending solutions, configuring Workday, solving complex issues, and continuously improving how we use the platform. 

What Success Looks Like 

You will thrive in this role if you: 

  • Think like a consultant. You seek to understand the business need behind a request and recommend the best solution. 
  • Bring solutions forward proactively. You stay curious about Workday capabilities, releases, emerging functionality, and leading practices and connect those opportunities to real business needs. 
  • Balance leading practice with practicality. You understand how Workday is designed to operate while recognizing that solutions must work for our business, employees, and HR teams. 
  • Build strong partnerships. You work alongside COEs, HRBPs, HRIS colleagues, HRIT, and other stakeholders as a trusted and engaged partner in business discussions and solution design. 
  • Comfortable challenging and being challenged. You bring a thoughtful point of view, ask good questions, explore alternatives, and remain open to different perspectives. 
  • Own outcomes. You see work through, from problem definition and solution design to configuration, testing, implementation, and continuous improvement. 
  • Look beyond today’s request. You consider scalability, employee experience, data, downstream impacts, and future needs when designing solutions. 
  • A team-first problem solver. You share knowledge, collaborate across functional teams, and focus on finding the right answer, remaining open to approaches that best support shared goals. 

Key Responsibilities 

Workday Functional Ownership & Optimization 

  • Provide advanced functional expertise for Workday, with primary emphasis on Workday Advanced Compensation, and support across additional Workday areas as needed. 
  • Serve as a trusted HRIS partner for assigned HR functions, developing a strong understanding of their business processes, priorities, challenges, and opportunities. 
  • Translate business needs into scalable Workday solutions, configurations, reporting capabilities, and process improvements. 
  • Configure and optimize Workday functional modules, business processes, condition rules, validations, calculated fields, reporting, and security. 
  • Proactively identify opportunities to improve how ONEOK uses Workday, including capabilities available through Workday releases and emerging functionality. 
  • Evaluate Workday capabilities and leading practices and recommend solutions appropriate for ONEOK’s business environment. 
  • Evaluate and help implement AI-enabled Workday capabilities aligned with business needs and strategy. 

Consultative Partnership 

  • Partner closely with HR COEs, HRBPs, HRIS, IT, and business stakeholders to understand needs and develop solutions. 
  • Ask thoughtful questions to uncover the business problem, desired outcome, and downstream implications behind system requests. 
  • Provide recommendations and alternatives to help stakeholders evaluate the best path forward. 
  • Explain Workday capabilities, constraints, and options in business terms so stakeholders can make informed decisions. 
  • Build trusted relationships across HR and the organization through responsiveness, expertise, collaboration, and sound judgment. 
  • Coach COE partners on effective use of Workday and help build broader understanding of system capabilities. 

Troubleshooting & Continuous Improvement 

  • Independently analyze and resolve complex Workday system and process issues. 
  • Identify root causes and implement sustainable solutions that support long-term strategy. 
  • Analyze patterns in break/fix activity, requests, and business processes to identify opportunities for broader improvement. 
  • Balance immediate operational needs with longer-term optimization and scalability. 
  • Maintain appropriate functional documentation, configuration documentation, and audit support. 

Enhancements, Projects & Releases 

  • Own Workday enhancements and initiatives from requirements through implementation. 
  • Translate business requirements into functional specifications and system designs. 
  • Lead functional testing for Workday releases, enhancements, and configuration changes. 
  • Develop test scenarios and coordinate defect identification, resolution, and validation. 
  • Partner with stakeholders to validate solutions and obtain acceptance prior to release. 
  • Conduct post-implementation reviews and incorporate learnings into future solutions. 
  • Follow established governance, change management, release management, and Records and Information Management protocols. 

Integrations & Data 

  • Support troubleshooting of Workday integrations, including EIBs and vendor inbound/outbound processes. 
  • Partner with technical and data teams to identify and resolve integration and data-flow issues. 
  • Consider upstream and downstream impacts when designing Workday solutions and process changes. 

What You Bring 

Skills & Capabilities 

  • Strong Workday functional knowledge with the ability to independently evaluate, configure, troubleshoot, and optimize solutions. 
  • Strong knowledge in Workday Advanced Compensation, with broader familiarity across the Workday ecosystem. 
  • Demonstrated ability to operate as a consultative partner, combining technical expertise with business understanding. 
  • Ability to translate business challenges into thoughtful technology and process solutions. 
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including root-cause analysis. 
  • Demonstrated ability to research Workday capabilities, evaluate alternatives, and make clear recommendations. 
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to make complex technology concepts understandable to nontechnical audiences. 
  • Curiosity about new Workday functionality, emerging technology, and opportunities to continuously improve. 
  • Strong relationship-building skills and a collaborative, team-oriented approach. 
  • Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and independently drive work forward. 
  • High attention to detail and sound judgment when working with sensitive employee information. 

Experience 

  • 5–7 years of related Workday HRIS experience. 
  • Strong hands-on Workday experience, including requirements gathering, configuration, troubleshooting, testing, and release management. 
  • Demonstrated Workday Advanced Compensation configuration experience, including merit, STI, LTI, and allowance plans, annual compensation review cycles, business processes, eligibility rules, calculated fields, reporting and auditing, EIBs, and security. 
  • Advanced Workday reporting experience.
  • Strong job architecture knowledge and experience updating configuration.  
  • Experience partnering directly with HR customers and translating business needs into technology solutions. 
  • Broad understanding of HR processes and their relationships across areas such as compensation, benefits, payroll, recruiting, talent, learning, and reporting. 
  • Experience managing multiple priorities and delivering solutions in a fast-paced environment. 

Education 

  • Bachelor’s degree or a combination of formal education and relevant experience. 

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities 

  • Knowledge of: HR functional knowledge (ie: compensation, benefits, payroll, performance, recruiting, learning, reporting etc.) and applicable governmental laws/regulations 
  • Ability to: utilize strong interpersonal skills to successfully collaborate and provide consultative advice/communication across multiple teams and stakeholders 
  • Ability to: establish and maintain effective working relationships with all levels of employees and leadership 
  • Ability to: utilize strong communication skills and ability to present to peers and customers at all levels of the organization 
  • Ability to: utilize strong analytical skills to identify, troubleshoot and provide solutions 
  • Ability to: research and articulate solutions 
  • Ability to: be curious and desire to drive innovation 
  • Ability to: pay attention to detail 
  • Ability to: utilize a high attention to detail and maintain confidential data with discretion 
  • Ability to: utilize strong critical thinking skills 
  • Ability to: be proactive versus reactive 

Strength Factor Rating - Physical Demands/Requirements

  • Sedentary Work - Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally (Occasionally: activity or condition exists up to 1/3 of the time) and/or a negligible amount of force frequently (Frequently: activity or condition exists from 1/3 to 2/3 of the time) to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Sedentary work involves sitting most of the time, but may involve walking or standing for brief periods of time. Jobs are sedentary if walking and standing are required only occasionally and all other sedentary criteria are met.

Strength Factor Description - Physical Demands/Requirements

  • Walking: Moving about on foot (Frequently)
  • Sitting: Remaining in a seated position (Constantly)
  • Lifting: Raising or lowering an object from one level to another (includes upward pulling) (Occasionally)
  • Carrying: Transporting an object, usually holding it in the hands or arms, or on the shoulder (Occasionally)
  • Pushing: Exerting force upon an object so that the object moves away from the force (Occasionally)
  • Pulling: Exerting force upon an object so that the object moves toward the force (includes jerking) (Occasionally)
  • Climbing: Ladders, Stairs (Occasionally)
  • Balancing: Maintaining body equilibrium to prevent falling (Occasionally)
  • Stooping: Bending the body downward and forward by bending the spine at the waist (Occasionally)
  • Kneeling: Bending the legs at the knees to come to rest on the knee or knees (Occasionally)
  • Crouching: Bending the body downward and forward by bending the legs and spine (Occasionally)
  • Crawling: Moving about on the hands and arms in any direction (Occasionally)
  • Reaching: Extending hands and arms in any direction (Constantly)
  • Handling: Seizing, holding, grasping, turning or otherwise working with the hand or hands (Manual Dexterity) (Constantly)
  • Fingering: Picking, pinching or otherwise working with the fingers primarily (Finger Dexterity) (Constantly)
  • Feeling: Perceiving such attributes of objects/materials as size, shape, temperature, texture, movement or pulsation by receptors in the skin, particularly those of the finger tips (Constantly)
  • Talking: Expressing or exchanging ideas/information by means of the spoken word (Frequently)

  • Tasting/Smelling: (Occasionally)

  • Far Vision: Clarity of vision at 20 feet for more (Frequently)
  • Depth Perception: Three-dimensional vision; ability to judge distances and spatial relationships so as to see objects where and as they actually are (Frequently)
  • Vision: Color - The ability to identify and distinguish colors (Constantly)

Working Conditions/Environment

  • Employee is subject to inside environmental conditions

Working Conditions

  • Well lighted, climate controlled areas (Constantly)

Travel

Driving

Talent Acquisition Coordinator

Bertram Capital is a private equity firm targeting investments in lower middle market companies. Since its inception in 2006, the firm has raised over $4B of capital commitments. Bertram has distinguished itself in the private equity community by combining venture capital operating methodologies with private equity financial discipline to empower its portfolio companies to unlock their full business potential. This approach is unique in that Bertram is not singularly focused on achieving its investment returns through financial engineering and the extraction of near-term cash flow. Instead, Bertram focuses on reinvestment and technology enablement to drive growth and value through digital marketing, e-commerce, big data and analytics, application development and internal and external platform optimization.

Visit www.bcap.com for more information.

Location

This is a remote role.

  • Candidate must be based in one of the following states: California, Colorado, Idaho, Minnesota, Illinois, Massachusetts, Florida, New York, Wisconsin, Texas, Arizona, Indiana, or Ohio.
  • A hybrid work opportunity may be available for candidates based near Foster City, CA or Broomfield, CO.

About the Role

The Talent Acquisition coordinator will support the recruiting strategy for Bertram Capital and Bertram Labs. They will source and review candidates, conduct introductory interviews, and navigate qualified candidates through the interview process. Another function of this role is administrative support for the talent acquisition function including scheduling, updating documents, and summarizing information for multiple stakeholders.

The ideal candidate has experience in investment banking, technology, or private equity recruiting. This person will serve as a trusted partner to the Bertram team and as candidates’ first impression of Bertram’s culture. They are comfortable working in a fast-paced, confidential, and highly professional environment.

Responsibilities

  • Develop a deep understanding of the goals of the firm to identify candidates who are the right fit.
  • Review and source candidates using ATS, LinkedIn, and industry specific resources.
  • Contribute to a positive candidate experience, maintaining timely and informative communication throughout the process.
  • Conduct introductory interviews with candidates.
  • Record detailed and concise notes from interviews to be shared with multiple internal stakeholders.
  • Track candidates consistently as they progress through each interview stage.
  • Gather and document feedback from hiring team on each candidate to determine next steps.
  • Provide support for in-person recruiting events and interviews.
  • Ensure compliance with employment laws and maintain confidentiality throughout the hiring process.
  • Manage administrative duties that support the Talent Acquisition function.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university
  • 1–2 years of talent acquisition/human resources experience in a relevant industry
  • Experience in a highly confidential, fast-paced professional setting
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Exceptional detail orientation as well as interpersonal and organizational skills
  • Familiarity with applicant tracking systems or HRIS
  • AI forward approach to efficiency
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across multiple teams
  • Flexible, team player who will help, teach, and learn from others
  • Ability to represent the firm positively and model the Bertram brand with external stakeholders

Compensation and Benefits

The expected salary range for this position is: $90,000- $100,000 total annual compensation. Offered salary may be based on a variety of factors including skills, experience, and qualifications for the role. Other compensation includes profit sharing.

Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits are provided at no cost to the employee. We offer a generous 401K match as well as a “take what you need” PTO policy.

If hired, employee will be in an “at-will position” and the Company reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company or individual department/team performance, and market factors.

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

At Bertram Capital we value and celebrate the many perspectives that arise from a variety of cultures, genders, religions, national origins, ages, abilities, socioeconomic status and sexual orientation. Our commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) ensures that Bertram is a place that attracts, grows, and promotes top talent from all backgrounds.

This is a senior individual-contributor role embedded within our Global Cybersecurity Operations team, with a primary focus on the Microsoft Purview platform and the broader suite of data and information protection controls that safeguard Intapp's most sensitive data assets.

This role sits at the intersection of security engineering, compliance, and data governance. In addition to the primary data protection mandate, the role provides critical backfill capability across both Corporate IT Security (endpoint and email security) and Cloud Security (vulnerability and posture management) functions within the SecOps team.


This role suits a security professional who combines deep Microsoft Purview technical expertise with a rigorous, policy-minded approach to data governance. You think in data flows, classification taxonomies, and risk — translating policy intent into enforced technical controls at scale. You are comfortable working autonomously, owning complex cross-functional workstreams, and communicating outcomes clearly to security leadership and business stakeholders.


Key Responsibilities:


  • Microsoft Purview & Data Protection: Own the administration and optimisation of Microsoft Purview, including sensitivity labels, data classification, retention policies, auditing, eDiscovery, and information protection across Microsoft 365 and Azure.
  • Data Loss Prevention (DLP): Design, implement, and continuously improve DLP policies across Microsoft 365, endpoints, and cloud environments. Investigate policy violations, manage incidents, and develop custom sensitive information classifiers.
  • Information Governance: Maintain enterprise data classification standards and information protection policies, ensuring alignment with regulatory requirements such as GDPR, CCPA, and ISO 27001. Monitor data protection effectiveness and provide governance reporting.
  • Security Operations Integration: Integrate Purview with Microsoft Sentinel, develop monitoring and analytics capabilities, and support insider risk investigations and data-related security incidents.

  • Familiarity with endpoint and email security tooling (e.g., Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Microsoft Defender for Office 365) is preferred; hands-on alert triage or policy administration experience is a plus.

  • Technical degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or related discipline.
  • Experience operating Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and/or Microsoft Defender for Office 365 in a SOC, IT security, or security engineering capacity.

  • Purview sensitivity label coverage at or above agreed enterprise target, with auto-labelling operational for key sensitive data types.
  • DLP policy framework deployed across Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, and Endpoint — with documented tuning cycle and false-positive rate within tolerance.

  • Vulnerability management and posture management backfill effective across Cloud Security — scan cadence maintained, remediation tracked, and posture reporting delivered to leadership.

jobs.excerpt: Who we are Bowery Valuation is one of the leading startups in the emerging world of real estate tech and the only company of its kind in the commercial real estate appraisal space.
jobs.description:
Who we are

Bowery Valuation is one of the leading startups in the emerging world of real estate tech and the only company of its kind in the commercial real estate appraisal space. We are also the first-ever venture capital-backed commercial appraisal firm, having raised over $80MM. Powered by big data, advanced technology, and extensive expertise, Bowery is redefining the entire commercial appraisal space.

Inside Bowery, we’re a people-forward company dedicated to providing a productive and inspiring working culture. We are a collection of hard-working and enthusiastic types focused on building great teams to support great work. We balance our dedication to success with a commitment to gratitude, kindness, and a team-first attitude.

About the Role

Bowery is in a new phase: rethinking the whole appraisal process with AI at the core. We’re hiring a Software Engineer to join our AI-first engineering team, reporting to our Head of Technology.

As the first truly tech-enabled appraisal firm - having raised over $80mm backed by Goldman Sachs, Capital One, and numerous venture funds - Bowery has a strong foundation to build on: a proprietary appraisal-writing platform, high-quality data, and a team of 100+ appraisers across 17 offices from more than 1,000 clients. We’ve grown over 30% year-over-year and are fully profitable.

Few industries are better suited for AI than appraisal. The work is structured, repetitive, and data-driven, and it pulls from fragmented sources. We want to use AI to turbocharge appraisers, who can spend their time on judgment, comparables, and compliance instead of data entry. The result will be a better product for our clients and a transformation in the industry.

This is a senior engineering role, not a prompt-writing role. We want someone with a strong software engineering foundation who also uses AI tools like Claude Code and Codex to get far more done than they could alone. You’ll make product decisions, own systems end to end, and hold a high bar for how they’re built.

Bowery is a post-Series B company with clear product-market fit and material scale, but with a small engineering team. You get the security and data of a late-stage startup with the impact of a very early one.

What You’ll Do

  • Design, build, and ship features end to end across our appraisal platform and AI-powered workflows, from data extraction and analysis to narrative generation
  • Work directly with appraisers and Ops to understand the problem, decide what to build, and make the product calls to get it shipped
  • Use AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, or similar) every day, and help shape how the team uses them well, including knowing where not to trust them
  • Build LLM-backed features with evaluation, testing, and monitoring in place so quality is measured, not guessed at
  • Own infrastructure and deployments on AWS, including CI/CD with GitHub Actions, infrastructure as code with Terraform, and containerized services with Docker
  • Keep the bar high on system design, code review, testing, and observability as we move faster

Experience and Skills

  • 4+ years building and shipping production software, ideally including time at an early-stage or fast-moving company
  • Strong fundamentals in system design, data modeling, APIs, and testing
  • Fluent in TypeScript and Node.js; React experience is a plus
  • AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, or similar) are a real part of how you work today, and you have opinions on how to use them without giving up quality
  • Experience building with LLMs: prompt design, RAG, structured outputs, and evals
  • Experience with AWS preferred, along with GitHub Actions, Terraform, and Docker

Why You’d Be a Good Fit

  • You want ownership. You’d rather figure out what should be built than wait for a fully specced ticket, and you’re comfortable making and defending product decisions.
  • You think critically. You use AI to multiply your output, and you review its work the way you’d review a teammate’s. You know when something is good enough to ship and when it isn’t.
  • You care how things are built. Speed matters, but so do clean interfaces, tests, and systems that the next engineer can understand.
  • You enjoy having direct access to end users. Our core users (appraisers and Ops teams) are all in-house, so you’d be iterating with a tight feedback loop. Many of them work 3x/week from our office in Cooper Square.
  • You value a remote-first eng culture. Our engineers prioritize async communication and make space for deep focus time to help us ship faster.

Why You Might Not Be a Good Fit

  • You want well-defined tickets and a narrow scope. This role means wearing many hats and working through ambiguity with the business.
  • You’d rather not use AI tools in your work. They’re central to how our team operates and how we expect to scale.
  • You’d ship code you don’t understand. AI-generated code still needs to meet our engineering standards, and you own what you merge.

Bowery’s Tech Stack

  • Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript
  • Frontend: React
  • Backend: Node.js (NestJS framework)
  • Database: MongoDB, Postgres
  • Infrastructure: AWS, Docker, Terraform, GitHub Actions

Bowery Leadership

  • John Meadows, Chief Executive Officer; LinkedIn
  • Madeline Pinkner, Head of Technology; LinkedIn
  • Eliot Jenkins, President and Chief Operating Officer; LinkedIn
  • Steve Schaller, Chief Revenue Officer; LinkedIn

jobs.title: Customer Success Engineer (Canada)
jobs.excerpt: Description We're looking for a hands-on Customer Success Engineer who owns customer relationships, drives customer outcomes, and enjoys solving complex data problems.
jobs.description:
Description

We're looking for a hands-on Customer Success Engineer who owns customer relationships, drives customer outcomes, and enjoys solving complex data problems.

We're taking a different approach to Customer Success. Rather than primarily coaching customers on how to use Insycle, our team works directly in their environments to investigate problems, build solutions, and deliver results. Think of it as Customer Success with a Forward Deployed Engineer mindset.

With our secure Support Access, you'll be able to configure and test solutions directly in customers' Insycle environments. Customers retain control over approving and executing changes to their CRM data.

You'll own a portfolio of customers across onboarding, ongoing adoption, renewals, and expansion. You'll build relationships, understand customers' business challenges, and help them get lasting value from Insycle.

This role combines hands-on technical problem-solving with customer relationships and business understanding. You'll have the autonomy to investigate challenges, design practical solutions, and see your work make a difference.

Location: Remote. We're looking for candidates based in the Eastern or Central time zones who can collaborate effectively with our team and customers during U.S. business hours.

What you’ll do

Solve customer data challenges

  • Understand customers' business goals and translate their requirements into practical data solutions.
  • Investigate CRM records, fields, workflows, and existing configurations to understand problems and identify root causes.
  • Configure Blueprints, templates, matching rules, transformations, associations, assignments, and other Insycle capabilities on customers' behalf.
  • Test solutions against real customer data, review previews, investigate edge cases, and refine configurations until they produce the expected results.
  • Choose simple, reliable solutions that customers can understand and maintain, and follow through to ensure the original problem is resolved.

Drive adoption and customer outcomes

  • Lead customer onboarding, configuring initial use cases and helping customers achieve results quickly.
  • Help customers move from one-time cleanup to continuous data integrity using Blueprints, Data Logic, and Observability.
  • Proactively review customer usage, identify opportunities to improve workflows, and recommend additional use cases.
  • Monitor adoption, address challenges early, and help customers get sustained value from Insycle.

Build relationships and grow accounts

  • Own customer relationships across onboarding, ongoing use, renewals, and expansion.
  • Become a trusted partner by understanding customers' priorities, offering practical recommendations, and following through.
  • Identify opportunities to expand Insycle usage across teams, CRM objects, and business processes.
  • Communicate business value through measurable results, including time saved, data quality improvements, and reduced operational risk.
  • Proactively manage customer relationships, identify adoption and retention risks, initiate outreach when intervention is needed, and help customers achieve the outcomes that support renewal and growth.

Improve how we work

  • Share knowledge, document reusable solutions, and collaborate with teammates to solve challenging problems.
  • Identify recurring customer issues and contribute ideas to improve the product, onboarding, and customer experience.
  • Use AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude to investigate problems, explore solutions, and improve workflows, while validating the results.
  • Take initiative to improve processes, learn from feedback, and help the team become more effective.

Requirements

  • Relevant experience: You have 3+ years of experience in technical Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Consulting, Implementation, RevOps, or a similar customer-facing B2B SaaS role.
  • Customer account ownership: You have experience directly managing ongoing customer relationships or a portfolio of accounts, taking responsibility for customer outcomes, adoption, and retention—not solely responding to technical support requests.
  • Technical problem-solving: You enjoy investigating complex problems, working with data, asking thoughtful questions, and finding practical solutions.
  • CRM and data experience: You're comfortable with HubSpot, Salesforce, or similar platforms, including data management, business rules, workflows, and automation.
  • Ownership and initiative: You work independently, take responsibility for outcomes, and follow through without needing constant direction.
  • Customer communication: You can explain technical concepts clearly, understand business needs, and build strong customer relationships.
  • Judgment and attention to detail: You think through consequences, validate your work, and favor simple, reliable solutions.
  • Teamwork and growth: You enjoy collaborating, sharing knowledge, learning from feedback, and helping the team improve.

Experience with CRM data quality, deduplication, data transformation, record matching, or integrations is a plus. Software development experience is not required.

Why join Insycle

You'll work on real data challenges across a wide range of customers and industries, with the tools and autonomy to investigate problems and build solutions yourself. You'll see the results of your work directly and build strong relationships with the people you help.

We're a small team with an established product and ambitious plans. You'll have the opportunity to influence how we serve customers, improve our product, and help shape the next stage of Insycle's growth.

How we work

Our values shape how we work together, make decisions, and develop as a team:

  • Care deeply: Understand customers' needs and take initiative to help them succeed.
  • Everyone builds: Look for opportunities to improve how we work and contribute practical solutions.
  • Better together: Share knowledge, support teammates, and work toward shared success.
  • Quality counts: Think through the details, validate your work, and deliver reliable results.
  • Positive energy: Bring kindness, constructive communication, and a willingness to tackle challenges.
  • Own the outcome: Take responsibility, follow through, and deliver results.
  • Choose simplicity: Favor practical, reliable solutions over unnecessary complexity.
  • Raise the bar: Seek feedback, keep learning, and help others improve.

Compensation and benefits

  • Annual base salary of CAD $90,000 - $115,000, depending on relevant experience and location.
  • Annual performance-based bonus with a target of 10% of base salary.
  • Equity through stock options.
  • Paid time off, sick leave, flexibility for unexpected needs, and paid holidays.

Company Overview

Insycle builds data integrity infrastructure for the agentic CRM. More than 700 customers trust our tools to resolve duplicates, standardize data, manage imports, and connect related records in platforms such as HubSpot and Salesforce.

Those tools fix what’s wrong today. But clean data is a moment. Data integrity is a system.

Our platform helps businesses define what right looks like in Blueprints, continuously apply those standards through Data Logic, and use Observability to understand where data conforms, where it drifts, and whether it stays aligned over time.

As AI agents increasingly use CRM data to make decisions and write changes back, that foundation becomes essential. Businesses need reliable inputs and a system that detects when people, integrations, workflows, or agents move data away from their standards.

We’re a B2B SaaS company with an established customer base and a much larger ambition: to make data integrity foundational to how businesses operate with AI.

jobs.excerpt: Grants Acquisition and Management Specialist Job Title: Grants Acquisition and Management Specialist Employment Type: W-2 Full-Time Reports to: Chief Executive Officer Location: Remote, Virginia-based, with occasional travel to Hampton Roads and partner districts as needed Schedule: Full-time (40 hours per week), Monday–Friday, during business hours, Eastern Time.
jobs.description:
Grants Acquisition and Management Specialist

Job Title: Grants Acquisition and Management Specialist

Employment Type: W-2 Full-Time

Reports to: Chief Executive Officer

Location: Remote, Virginia-based, with occasional travel to Hampton Roads and partner districts as needed

Schedule: Full-time (40 hours per week), Monday–Friday, during business hours, Eastern Time. Grant deadlines may occasionally require additional hours.

Compensation: $85,000 per year (salary)

About Virtual Peace of Mind (VPM)

Virtual Peace of Mind (VPM) is a fast-growing, fully remote mental health practice dedicated to providing evidence-based mental health services to children, adults, and families across multiple states. Our mission is to expand equitable access to mental health services through high-quality virtual care — and to support the clinicians and professionals who make that care possible.

We're building a culture that is mission-driven, accountable, supportive, and built for sustainable remote work.

Why Join VPM

At VPM, you'll be part of a team transforming access to mental health care through virtual care — with a remote model designed to support excellent work and real life.

What you can expect:

  • Mission-Driven Impact: Contribute to meaningful work improving access to mental health care for youth and families, including students in rural Virginia school districts.
  • Remote by Design: Fully remote environment with clear expectations and supportive infrastructure, with occasional travel.
  • Collaborative Culture: Work with a multidisciplinary team that values integrity, empathy, and shared learning.
  • Growth & Leadership Pathways: Opportunities to expand scope and take on leadership responsibilities as we scale.
  • Professional Development: Access to training, resources, and continued learning opportunities aligned to role scope.
  • State & School-Based Partnerships: Join initiatives that strengthen school-based mental health delivery and expand access across communities.

Role Overview

VPM is seeking a Grants Acquisition and Management Specialist to lead the grant work that fuels VPM's growth: finding funding that fits VPM's school-based mental health programs, writing the applications, getting them submitted on time, and managing awarded grants through spending, reporting, and closeout. This is the role that keeps VPM's expansion engine running — grants are how VPM enters new school districts and keeps school-based services at no cost to students and families.

The Grants Acquisition and Management Specialist owns the grant pipeline end to end: tracking open and upcoming opportunities (including the Virginia Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), the Virginia Foundation for Healthy Youth (VFHY), and the annual DBHDS school-based mental health grants), checking eligibility against the districts VPM serves, drafting narratives and budgets with the CEO and clinical and finance leads, assembling attachments, and submitting before the deadline. Once a grant is awarded, this role manages it — tracking spending against the budget, preparing financial and progress reports, meeting reporting deadlines, and keeping VPM in compliance with funder requirements. This person also builds VPM's grants tracking system from the ground up — a funding dashboard where leadership can see every funding source, its status, and what's moving — so that when awards land, the money drops into a system that is already built and ready.

This is an organization-wide role supporting VPM's private practice, school-based programs, and other approved initiatives. The Grants Acquisition and Management Specialist works closely with the CEO and with clinical, finance, and community engagement leads.

Ideal Candidate Profile

We are seeking someone who:

  • Writes clearly and well — they can turn program details into a compelling, accurate grant narrative without a lot of back-and-forth.
  • Knows the government grant world — they have written federal, state, or local grant applications before and can show funded awards.
  • Is organized and can manage multiple applications and deadlines at once, without letting one slip.
  • Is self-directed — they see what needs doing and do it, without waiting to be told.
  • Pays attention to detail — they check figures, dates, eligibility rules, and submission requirements before anything goes out.
  • Understands the mission — they care about access to mental health care and want their work to mean something.
  • Can work with numbers — they can build and check a grant budget with the CEO and finance leads.
  • Is comfortable on both sides of the work — they can chase a new opportunity and also keep the books straight on one already won.
  • Builds systems, not just paperwork — they can create the tracking and reporting tools VPM needs from scratch, including a funding dashboard leadership can actually use.

Who This Role Is Not For

This role is not a good fit for someone who:

  • Misses deadlines or needs to be chased to finish a submission.
  • Writes in generalities and cannot back claims with specific numbers and sources.
  • Wants a role with fixed, repetitive tasks rather than a changing pipeline of opportunities.
  • Is uncomfortable asking the CEO and clinical leads for the program details a strong application needs.
  • Cannot keep careful track of what each application committed to, so later reports match what was promised.

Key Responsibilities

  • Find funding: Track grant opportunities that fit VPM's school-based and virtual mental health programs, including RHTP regional programs, VFHY, and the annual DBHDS school-based mental health grants; flag new RFAs, deadline changes, and new guidance.
  • Check the fit: Verify eligibility for each opportunity — which districts and populations VPM serves, what the funder will and will not pay for, and whether the timeline is realistic.
  • Write the applications: Draft grant narratives, work plans, and budgets with the CEO and relevant leads; assemble cover sheets, certifications, financial statements, licenses, and other attachments.
  • Mind the numbers: Make sure every figure in an application is verified and consistent across the narrative, work plan, and budget before submission.
  • Submit on time: Own the submission calendar and checklist for each application, including portal submissions and emailed PDFs, and confirm receipt.
  • Track the pipeline: Maintain a grant calendar and status tracker — what is open, what is due, what is submitted, what is awarded, and what comes next.
  • Build the funding dashboard: Create and maintain a grants dashboard that shows every funding source — what's open, what's submitted, what's awarded, what's spent, and what's due — so leadership can see the full funding picture at a glance.
  • Manage awarded grants: Track spending against each grant budget, prepare financial and progress reports, meet all reporting deadlines, and keep VPM in compliance with funder requirements.
  • Maintain grant records: Keep complete grant files — applications, budgets, awards, reports, and correspondence — so every commitment VPM made can be accounted for.

Performance & Accountability

  • Funding pipeline maintained and current, with opportunities evaluated and deadlines met.
  • Applications submitted complete and on time.
  • Awarded grants tracked accurately, with financial and progress reports submitted on schedule.
  • Funding dashboard built and kept current.
  • Weekly activity report to the CEO — what was accomplished, what opportunities were evaluated, which applications advanced, what deadlines are approaching, and what decisions are needed.

Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience writing government grant applications — federal, state, or local — with funded awards to show for it, preferably in health care, education, or behavioral health.
  • Strong writing, editing, and research skills.
  • Experience building or checking budgets for grant applications.
  • Experience managing awarded grants, including financial tracking, progress and financial reporting, and funder compliance.
  • Familiarity with federal grants compliance (2 CFR 200 / Uniform Guidance) is a plus.
  • Familiarity with Virginia health and education funding, rural health programs, or school-based services is a plus.
  • Comfortable working in Google Drive, grant portals, and email; able to learn new systems quickly.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.

Tools & Systems

Google Drive, Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel/Google Sheets, grant submission portals (including Grants.gov and SAM.gov), and email.

Employment Process

  1. Submit application.
  2. Selected applicants will be contacted for an initial interview.
  3. Notification to submit a grant writing sample (redacted samples are acceptable) and walk through a past application (what the opportunity was, how you approached it, and the outcome).
  4. Second interview with the CEO and relevant leads.
  5. Invitation to join if selected.

Benefits & Time Off (W-2 Eligible Roles)

VPM supports your well-being with benefits designed for health, stability, and real work-life balance.

Health, Dental & Vision: Company-sponsored plans available, with an employer contribution for eligible full-time employees.
Quick Benefits Start: Benefits eligibility begins after 30 days, with coverage effective the first of the month following Day 30.
Flexible Holidays: No fixed holiday calendar—team members are empowered to plan schedules and observe holidays meaningful to them.

Eligibility: Benefits are available to full-time employees (40 hours/week).

Equal Employment Opportunity

Virtual Peace of Mind is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive, equitable environment for all employees. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Reasonable Accommodation & Accessibility

Virtual Peace of Mind is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and applicants with disabilities. If you require accommodation to complete the application process, participate in an interview, or perform essential job functions, please contact HR at to request assistance. All accommodation requests are handled confidentially and in accordance with applicable law. If qualified for a role, our talent acquisition team will contact you. Please only reach out if accommodation with the application/interviewing process is required.

Employment Eligibility & Compliance

All offers of employment are contingent upon the successful completion of a background check and eligibility to work in the United States without company-sponsorship. VPM complies fully with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination, confidentiality, and data privacy, including HIPAA, FERPA, and state-specific clinical/employment regulations.

  • Drive standardization and automation of configuration, bring-up, validation, and documentation activities to improve repeatability as the organization scales.

jobs.excerpt: Company Overview At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.


Department Overview

At Motorola Solutions, we are committed to "Solving for safer" by building and connecting technologies that help protect people, property, and places. Our Infrastructure Operations team stands behind the mission-critical platforms that emergency services rely on when every second counts, including Guardian, our 999 and 101 call-taking and dispatching solution, and Pronto, our digital notebook service empowering frontline police officers across the UK and Europe. Working across specialized networking, virtualisation, and infrastructure streams, we collaborate to keep our hosted environments resilient, secure, and ready for the moments that matter.

Join our Shared Platform services team as a Network Engineer, where you will be instrumental in the planning, designing and implementation of new networking solutions all whilst providing critical support for existing infrastructure. These solutions have multiple products deemed as critical national infrastructure and operate on an Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) platform.

About the products you will support:

Guardian is a call taking & dispatching platform used by emergency service operators across the UK & Europe. We help 999 or 101 operators answer calls from the public and dispatch out nearby responders, enabling the right response when every second counts, and ultimately helping our customers save lives.

Pronto is a digital notebook service providing front line police officers with access to national systems to obtain information quickly and efficiently when working within their communities. Pronto also allows for digital evidence collection which can be used as evidence in juridical processes, location services for fast dispatching of officers, and a range of many other tools to aid in an officers day to day activities


Job Description

Everything starts with our people, and as a Network Engineer, you will join a people-first culture where your technical expertise directly impacts community safety. You will play a vital role in a fast-paced environment undergoing major infrastructure evolution over the next year, balancing innovative transformation projects with the demanding Service Level Agreements of our live public safety solutions. We value diverse backgrounds and equivalent practical experience, empowering you to pursue your passion, embrace continuous learning, and grow your career alongside a supportive, close-knit team. Whether working remotely or traveling to UK and international sites, you will bring strong communication skills and collaborative energy to connect those in need with those who can help.


Key Responsibilities

  • Manage and support end-to-end networking operations across multiple Motorola Solutions sites and remote customer locations to help deliver high availability for mission-critical emergency services.
  • Administer, review, and maintain firewall rulesets, routing policies, NAT configurations, and security objects across diverse multi-vendor environments.
  • Design, update, and maintain comprehensive network documentation and topology diagrams to support operational clarity and rapid incident resolution.
  • Collaborate with third-party vendors and internal Incident Management teams to troubleshoot and resolve circuit faults, outages, and complex routing issues.
  • Conduct capacity planning, performance tuning, and network optimization while participating in an on-call rotation (beginning after six months of service).
  • Help to provide strict compliance with public sector security policies and regulatory frameworks, including ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials, and NCSC security best practices.
  • Travel to internal and customer sites across the UK (with occasional international travel) as required to support infrastructure deployments and maintenance.


Basic Requirements

Must hold or have the ability to attain NPPV3 and SC clearance (requires a minimum of 5 years of UK residency).


  • Solid hands-on experience in a network engineering role supporting enterprise or multi-site infrastructures.
  • Full professional fluency in English (written and spoken) to collaborate across teams and document technical architectures.

Network Infrastructure


  • Layer 2 and Layer 3 networking expertise (VLANs, subnetting, STP, OSPF, and BGP) to design, maintain, and troubleshoot multi-site routing topologies, routing loops, asymmetric routing, and route redistribution.
  • Enterprise switching and WAN technologies experience (Aruba, Cisco, HP, or Juniper switches, private circuits, DIA, IPsec over internet, and EWLs) to manage reliable site connectivity.
  • Multi-site firewall and VPN administration proficiency (Fortinet or Check Point, static/dynamic NAT, PAT, UTM, IDS/IPS, IPsec, IKEv2, and route-based VPNs) to uphold operational security standards.
  • Packet capture and network observation tools experience (Wireshark, Grafana, Prometheus, SolarWinds, or FortiAnalyzer) to analyze traffic, diagnose connectivity issues, and apply security best practices.

Preferred Qualifications (Nice-to-Haves)

  • Experience configuring and managing SD-WAN solutions (specifically Fortinet SD-WAN), including overlay/underlay architecture, path selection, and link monitoring.
  • Hands-on familiarity with SIP technologies to support voice and critical communications traffic.
  • Experience working with Software-Defined Networking (SDN) platforms such as VMware NSX, Cisco ACI, or OVN.
  • Exposure to Red Hat OpenShift environments and containerized infrastructure networking.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to articulate complex network concepts clearly to technical peers, non-technical stakeholders, and public sector customers.
  • Adaptability and eagerness to learn emerging technologies while maintaining high standards under strict SLA pressures.

In return for your expertise, we’ll support you in this new challenge with coaching & development every step of the way. Also, to reward your hard work you’ll get:


  • Competitive salary and bonus schemes
  • Two weeks additional pay per year (holiday bonus).
  • 25 days holiday entitlement + bank holidays.
  • Attractive defined contribution pension scheme.
  • Company Car Scheme
  • Private medical insurance.
  • Employee stock purchase plan.
  • Flexible working options.
  • Life assurance.
  • Enhanced maternity and paternity pay.
  • Career development support and wide ranging learning opportunities.
  • Employee health and wellbeing support EAP, wellbeing guidance etc.
  • Carbon neutral initiatives/goals.
  • Corporate social responsibility initiatives including support for volunteering days.
  • Well known companies discount schemes.

Under 10%

None

Experienced

Yes

We are proud of our people-first and community-focused culture, empowering every Motorolan to be their most authentic self and to do their best work to deliver on the promise of a safer world. At T-Mobile, we invest in YOU! Our Total Rewards Package ensures that employees get the same big love we give our customers. All team members receive a competitive base salary and compensation package - this is Total Rewards. Employees enjoy multiple wealth-building opportunities through our annual stock grant, employee stock purchase plan, 401(k), and access to free, year-round money coaches. That’s how we’re UNSTOPPABLE for our employees!

The Sr. Strategy and Programs Manager, FWA HSI Local Marketing Activation is the connection between FWA High Speed Internet local marketing strategy and what happens in market. This role owns how local marketing gets activated for FWA HSI: partnering with the HSI acquisition team to identify opportunities and priorities, deciding where, why, and how to activate, designing the programs that do it, and enabling the field to run those programs with confidence.

The role works where network capacity and demand are out of balance. That includes High Supply and Low Demand markets, where available capacity isn’t converting into activations, and markets where churn and disconnects are eroding growth. This person turns market-level data into targeted local programs, runs them, measures them, and scales what works.

This is not a project coordinator role. This person builds the activation programs, owns their delivery, and is accountable for whether they drive new accounts and retention in market.

This is a remote role. Travel expectation is up to 30% nationally, covering market visits, National Marketing engagements, planning sessions, and team collaboration. The best activation programs are designed by people who spend time in the markets they are building.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES


Activation Strategy & Program Design

  • Own the activation approach. Develop the framework for how FWA HSI local marketing gets activated: which markets, which audiences, which tactics, in what sequence, and what principles guide local decisions.
  • Lead High Supply and Low Demand programs. Combine network capacity data with local marketing levers to build programs that convert available capacity into activation and define when a geography qualifies.
  • Build complete program designs. Every program should have a clear objective, target audience, channel mix, offer and messaging direction, timeline, budget, and success metric, with rationale for each choice.
  • Develop retention-oriented programs. Partner with the disconnect and churn effort to design local programs that reduce HSI churn, not just drive new orders.
  • Close the gaps. Identify moments where the organization lacks a proven tactic or a defined approach for FWA HSI, and build the solution instead of flagging it for someone else.

Program Execution & Field Enablement

  • Run the programs. Own program management from design through launch and close-out: timelines, dependencies, vendors, budgets, and cross-functional deliverables.
  • Enable the field. Give the field everything it needs to execute: program briefs, targeting lists, messaging guidance, creative assets, and clear success criteria.
  • Sequence the rollout. Pilot first, then scale in phases, tied to the commercial calendar and to the team’s 2027 expansion into HSI.
  • Make it stick. Partner with the Hyperlocal Playbook Manager so proven programs are captured in the playbook as operating standards.

Measurement & Test-and-Learn

  • Design the tests. Build test-and-control structures for local programs so the team can separate real lift from noise.
  • Target with data. Use propensity and segmentation analysis to choose and size markets and opportunity.
  • Report what works. Produce clear readouts on incremental new accounts, churn impact, cost per acquisition, and program ROI, and recommend scale, adjust, or stop.
  • Close the loop. Run a retrospective at the end of each program and each quarter: what the program produced, where execution diverged from the plan, and what changes next.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner with National Marketing. Pull national campaigns, brand guardrails, and creative into field-ready formats, and push field learnings back up so what gets built centrally serves local needs.
  • Partner with HSI Acquisition team to identify commercial opportunities and priorities for hyperlocal marketing campaigns
  • Partner with Network and Capacity Planning. Get timely, usable capacity data so programs target the right markets at the right time.
  • Partner with Analytics and Sales Operations. Align on data, measurement, and incentives so programs are measurable and the frontline is incented to action off of them.
  • Coordinate with the Fiber team. Manage the places where FWA and fiber overlap, including footprint eligibility changes and creating an ecosystem accounting for customer moves from HSI to fiber.
  • Steward the brand. Ensure local activity stays within T-Mobile brand guardrails while remaining locally effective.

Quarterly Planning & Field Intelligence

  • Contribute to the planning cycle. Translate commercial targets, capacity conditions, and national priorities into a 90-day activation program plan with market-by-market priorities.
  • Synthesize the signal. Aggregate market observations, competitive activity, and program performance into insights that inform local decisions and national direction.
  • Find the pattern. Identify which market conditions, audiences, and tactic combinations are producing results and what the team should do more of.
  • Brief leadership. Produce a regular update for the Sr. Manager and Director on what’s working, what isn’t, and what the field needs.

QUALIFICATIONS


  • Bachelor's Degree and 7 years of related work experience, or a combination of education and experience deemed equivalent
  • 7-10 years in marketing strategy, field marketing, growth marketing, or program management, with demonstrated ownership of programs from design through measurement.
  • Strong analytical skills, including campaign measurement, segmentation, and test-and-control design.
  • Experience managing complex, cross-functional programs with many stakeholders and no direct authority.
  • Experience translating strategy into field-executable programs that people actually use.
  • Strong written and verbal communicator who can brief the field, partner teams, and senior leaders.
  • Comfortable operating without complete information and adjusting quickly when results come in.
  • Experience in telecom, broadband, or a brand with a significant field or local marketing component preferred
  • Background managing the interface between a national marketing organization and a distributed field team preferred
  • Familiarity with hyperlocal marketing channels — OOH, community partnerships, ambassador programs, geo-targeted digital preferred
  • Experience developing audience segmentation frameworks and channel-audience matching strategies preferred
  • Background in capability building — has developed training, toolkits, or frameworks adopted by a field team preferred
  • At least 18 years of age
  • Legally authorized to work in the United States

Travel required

jobs.description:
AboutClient:
﻿﻿Hiring for our client providing end-to-end Facebook advertising services that scale e-commerce brands from $50,000 per month in revenue up to $1,000,000 per month.

The Result We Are Hiring For

We are hiring a LinkedIn growth consultant with one job: make LinkedIn a measurable, predictable source of booked sales meetings and closed revenue for our company within 60 days.

This is not a content or branding role. This is a revenue role. Every recommendation, audit, and training session you deliver must trace back to one of two outcomes: more qualified meetings booked, or more deals closed from LinkedIn-sourced leads.

We will manage this engagement directly against the KPIs listed in the Results section below. Extension of the contract beyond 60 days depends entirely on those numbers.

Role Overview

We are seeking a fractional LinkedIn consultant who has personally generated millions of dollars in revenue from LinkedIn leads to provide strategic direction, auditing, and hands-on training to our existing in-house LinkedIn specialist.

The primary purpose of this role is knowledge transfer. You will train and level up our in-house LinkedIn specialist until they can run the upgraded system independently. You will also work independently on audits and strategy, but the measure of your success is a department that performs without you needing to be in the weeds every day.

  • Engagement type: Independent consultant / contractor (fractional)
  • Time commitment: Approximately 5 hours per week (remote, flexible scheduling)
  • Contract term: 60 days initially, with extension based on results
  • Working model: Fully remote, online collaboration (daily syncs, weekly leadership meeting, Loom reviews, shared documents)

- Reports to: Founder / CEO

Responsibilities

  • You will own the strategy and quality control of our LinkedIn lead generation system while training our existing team member to execute it at a high level. Specifically:
  • Train and coach our existing in-house LinkedIn specialist through a daily sync, weekly working sessions, message reviews, and direct feedback. This is the primary objective of the engagement.
  • Audit our current LinkedIn outbound sequences (connection requests, follow-up messages, and cadence) and rewrite or direct rewrites where conversion is leaking.
  • Audit and sharpen our ICP qualification criteria so that only financially qualified, decision-maker prospects (e-commerce brand owners doing at least $50,000 per month in revenue) enter and progress through the funnel.
  • Review and improve our targeting, list building, and prospecting workflows to ensure we are reaching in-market buyers, not just titles.
  • Audit the full path from first touch to booked meeting, including profile positioning, message-to-call conversion, and calendar booking flow.
  • Document and upgrade our systems and procedures (SOPs) so the LinkedIn department runs on repeatable process, not individual effort.
  • Review weekly performance data, diagnose bottlenecks in the funnel, and issue clear corrective actions.
  • Ensure the department hits meeting booking targets and that booked meetings convert into sales opportunities that close.

Requirements

  • Proven, verifiable track record of generating millions of dollars in closed revenue from LinkedIn-sourced leads (you will be asked to substantiate this with case studies, references, or results data).
  • Deep expertise in LinkedIn outbound: sequence architecture, copywriting for cold outreach, ICP qualification, and list building.
  • Experience building or fixing LinkedIn lead generation systems inside real companies, not just personal brands.
  • Demonstrated ability to train and level up in-house operators (teaching skill, not just doing skill).
  • Strong diagnostic ability: can read funnel data, identify the bottleneck metric, and prescribe the fix.
  • Comfortable working in a fractional capacity with clear accountability to weekly KPIs.

Excellent written and verbal communication in English; able to deliver clear, actionable feedback asynchronously (Loom, docs) and live.

  • Reliability: consistent daily availability for the full 60-day term, including the daily sync.

Results Section (How We Will Measure This Engagement)

This section defines the KPIs we will manage the engagement against. The consultant is expected to move these numbers within the 60-day term.

Primary result: A minimum of 3-4 qualified sales meetings booked from LinkedIn every 30 days. This is a floor, not a cap; exceeding it is encouraged and rewarded through commission.

Secondary result: Closed revenue attributable to LinkedIn-sourced leads. Our engagement is a $5,000 one-time upfront retainer, so the target is $10,000 to $12,000 in closed revenue within the engagement window (two to three closed deals), or a clearly documented pipeline that closes within 30 days after the term ends.

  • Sequence performance: Measurable improvement in connection acceptance rate, reply rate, and positive-reply rate on outbound sequences versus the pre-engagement baseline.
  • Lead quality: Increase the percentage of booked meetings that meet ICP qualification criteria to 50-60% of all booked meetings.
  • Show rate: Improvement in booked-meeting show rate through improved pre-call positioning and follow-up.
  • Systems deliverables: Completed audit of sequences, ICP criteria, targeting, and funnel within the first 14 days; updated SOPs documented and in use by the in-house specialist by day 30.
  • Team capability: The in-house LinkedIn specialist can independently execute the upgraded system at standard by day 60. A baseline snapshot of all current metrics will be taken before the engagement begins so improvement is measured against real numbers, not opinions.

Working Structure

A daily sync of 15 to 30 minutes with the in-house LinkedIn specialist to train, review the previous day, and unblock whatever the specialist ran into that day.

One weekly one-hour strategy meeting that includes the in-house LinkedIn specialist and the Founder/CEO.

Asynchronous reviews of sequences, messages, and funnel assets via shared documents and Loom.

A short weekly written report: metrics versus KPIs, bottleneck identified, actions for the coming week.

Direct messaging access for quick questions during working days.

Commissions

10% one-time commission on each closed sale. Our client engagement is a $5,000 one-time upfront retainer, so each closed sale carries a $500 commission. Commission applies to deals closed within the engagement window and to deals that close within 30 days after the term ends.

Verifiable Results Requirement

Because this role is hired and paid against results, claims of revenue generated from LinkedIn must be substantiated. Applications that cannot demonstrate verifiable results will not be considered, regardless of profile quality or title. Before an interview is scheduled, candidates must submit:

At least two case studies with specific numbers: revenue generated, number of meetings booked, close rates, and the time period covered.

The full names and LinkedIn profiles of the clients or companies referenced in those case studies, so results can be independently confirmed.

At least one reference from a past client or employer who can speak directly to the LinkedIn results delivered. References will be contacted.

An example of an actual sequence, script, or system the candidate personally built, with the performance data behind it.

A short walkthrough (written or Loom) of how the candidate diagnosed and fixed a LinkedIn funnel that was underperforming.

During the interview process, candidates should expect direct questions about their numbers: where the leads came from, how attribution was tracked, and what portion of the claimed revenue was directly attributable to their work. Candidates who present results they cannot explain in detail will be disqualified.

Job Title: Enterprise Architect, Medicaid Management Information System (MMIS) Program
Work Arrangement: Fully remote within the United States; 35 to 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday between 7:45 AM and 4:30 PM Eastern Time (client working days only; no client holidays)
Location: Remote, United States (Eastern Time schedule)
Employment Type: W-2, 35 to 40 hours per week
Pay Rate: $60-$80/hr (W-2)
Engagement Type: Contract, January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2027, with possible extension
Final Interview: Client interview by phone or in person

Position Summary

Dhaka Technologies Limited Company is hiring an Enterprise Architect on behalf of the client, a state government agency, to support the state's Medicaid Management Information System (MMIS) program. The Enterprise Architect helps the state build a modern, responsive, stable and secure infrastructure for MMIS program work, providing guidance, recommendations and technical expertise on enterprise architecture processes and practices across the application, technology and information architecture domains.

The engagement covers architecture leadership, governance and technical deliverables across four workstreams: Governance and Agile Integration, DataOps Modernization, Microsoft Stack Expansion, and Legacy Workflow Retirement. The Enterprise Architect is a member of the state's Enterprise Architecture Office, reports to the Director of Enterprise Architecture, and works with state enterprise architects and solution providers.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop technology and architecture roadmaps and implementation plans, plus analysis and readiness plans for adopting new processes or technologies.
  • Produce enterprise reference and logical architecture diagrams (current and future state), integration architecture, system integration and data-flow diagrams, and architecture vision documentation for business partners.
  • Carry out architecture governance work and take part in the Enterprise Architecture Review Board or similar change control boards for architecture changes.
  • Prepare architecture gap analyses and document alternatives analyses when needed.
  • Advise the state on architecture changes to its Medicaid data warehouse and analytics platform, specifically data ingestion, data translation and data patterns.
  • Advise on architecture changes and target architecture designs for special investigations (SIU) case management, the second phase of interoperability, Medicaid Enterprise Systems (MES) and the unified health data space.
  • Advise on the target architecture for pharmacy benefits services, including working with the selected vendor on its offering.
  • Advise on the state health information exchange, with a focus on integration with state information systems.
  • Provide input to and review RFPs and contracts, support procurements by reviewing demonstrations and bid submissions, and support service level agreements with solution vendors and internal service providers.
  • Define infrastructure, application, cloud-services and data-services non-functional requirements, and review design documents (DDI).
  • Where needed, deliver Governance and Agile Integration architecture (enterprise governance architecture, architecture decision frameworks, Agile-enterprise integration architecture), DataOps Modernization architecture (data ingestion, entity resolution, data quality, lineage, metadata and semantic layer) and Legacy Workflow Retirement architecture (legacy system inventory and assessment, transition-state, decommissioning and cutover/rollback architecture).
  • Prepare CMS certification support artifacts when applicable, and provide data governance assistance on assigned projects.
  • Deliver a weekly status report and scrum to the Director of the Enterprise Architecture Office, and attend, and when appropriate lead, design sessions, steering committee meetings and project meetings.
  • Attend a monthly engagement meeting with the state's enterprise architecture staff, and other meetings when requested.
  • Work on state-provided tools: a state-issued computer, Microsoft Office, Microsoft Visio Professional and Azure DevOps.

Requirements

Required:

  • Experience working within an architecture framework such as TOGAF or FEAF.
  • Experience working within at least two architecture domains: business architecture, application architecture, information/data architecture and technology architecture.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills.
  • Ability to work within a team, meet shifting deadlines and work within a set budget.
  • Current annual cybersecurity awareness and HIPAA training certificates (copies are submitted to the client with your resume), or the ability to complete both before submission; the client's annual compliance training must also be completed and kept current during the engagement.
  • Three professional references, submitted with the application, who can speak to your enterprise architecture work.
  • Available 35 to 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday between 7:45 AM and 4:30 PM Eastern Time, for the full 12-month term.
  • Located in and authorized to work in the United States; work cannot be performed from outside the United States; W-2 only (no C2C or 1099).
  • Must pass a national criminal background check, sign the client's acceptable use and confidentiality terms, work only on client-provided systems, disclose any conflict of interest and any planned use of AI tools in the work, and not use AI meeting assistants in client meetings.

Preferred:

  • Enterprise architecture experience on state Medicaid programs, such as MMIS or Medicaid Enterprise Systems modernization, MITA and CMS certification.
  • Experience with health information exchange, pharmacy benefits systems, data warehouse or DataOps modernization, or Microsoft technology stack architecture.
  • TOGAF or a comparable architecture certification.
  • Prior work with a state central IT agency or enterprise architecture office.

How to Apply

Please send your resume, three professional references and copies of your certificates (TOGAF or other certifications listed on your resume, and your current HIPAA and cybersecurity awareness training certificates) to with "Enterprise Architect, MMIS" in the subject line. For each reference, include the name, title, organization, email address, phone number and the work the reference can speak to.

Job Description Summary

‎

Position Summary
The Chief of Staff serves as a trusted strategic advisor and operational partner to the Chief Executive Officer, helping maximize executive effectiveness while accelerating execution of Mosaic Health’s highest-priority strategic initiatives.

This is a highly visible leadership role responsible for driving enterprise coordination, executive operating cadence, strategic execution, transformation initiatives, and executive communications across the organization. Acting as an extension of executive leadership, the Chief of Staff ensures priorities are translated into action, cross-functional teams remain aligned, and critical initiatives are executed with discipline and urgency.

The successful candidate will thrive in a fast-paced, private equity-backed environment and possess the judgment, business acumen, and influence required to work effectively across executive leadership, Board members, business unit leaders, and external stakeholders. This role requires someone who is equally comfortable shaping strategy, solving complex operational challenges, and driving flawless execution.

‎

How will you make an impact & Requirements

‎

What You’ll Do

Executive Office Leadership

  • Serve as a trusted advisor and operational extension of the CEO, ensuring executive focus remains on the organization’s highest-value priorities.
  • Manage executive priorities by coordinating decisions, tracking commitments, and ensuring timely execution of follow-up actions.
  • Anticipate leadership needs and proactively resolve issues before they require executive intervention.
  • Prepare the CEO for Board meetings, sponsor interactions, customer meetings, investor discussions, and other strategic engagements.
  • Continuously improve executive workflows by identifying opportunities to leverage AI, automation, and technology to increase productivity.

Executive Leadership Team Effectiveness

  • Own and continuously improve the Executive Leadership Team’s operating cadence.
  • Develop executive meeting agendas, pre-read materials, action logs, decision trackers, and governance processes.
  • Ensure accountability for enterprise commitments through disciplined follow-up and progress tracking.
  • Connect priorities across business units and corporate functions to identify risks, dependencies, and opportunities.
  • Foster collaboration across the executive team while promoting transparency, alignment, and shared accountability.

Strategy Execution & Enterprise Initiatives

  • Translate executive priorities into actionable workplans with defined milestones, owners, timelines, and measurable outcomes.
  • Lead cross-functional strategic initiatives that span multiple business units or lack a natural organizational owner.
  • Partner with senior leaders to remove execution barriers and accelerate enterprise priorities.
  • Develop executive dashboards and progress reports that provide visibility into strategic initiatives and organizational performance.
  • Support annual strategic planning and enterprise prioritization activities.

Enterprise Transformation

  • Coordinate enterprise transformation initiatives in partnership with executive leadership.
  • Maintain executive project plans, governance documentation, milestone tracking, dependency management, and decision logs.
  • Support organizational redesign, business integration, and enterprise change management initiatives.
  • Ensure transformation efforts remain aligned with Mosaic Health’s strategic objectives and value creation plan.

Executive Communications & Board Support

  • Develop polished executive presentations, Board materials, sponsor updates, and strategic communications.
  • Improve the quality, clarity, and effectiveness of executive messaging across internal and external audiences.
  • Coordinate responses to Board members, investors, and private equity sponsors.
  • Ensure executives are equipped with high-quality materials that enable informed decision-making and effective stakeholder engagement.

Organizational Leadership

  • Build trusted relationships with executives, business leaders, and functional teams across Mosaic Health.
