Team Overview

The Corporate Strategy team develops the company’s strategy and translates it into action by leading TransUnion’s highest-priority, company-wide strategic and transformation initiatives that span businesses, functions and regions. Role Overview and Core Responsibilities

  • Lead a portfolio of the company’s most significant enterprise-wide strategy, growth and transformation initiatives, extending the capacity of the corporate strategy leadership team and operating primarily through influence.
  • Translate strategic priorities into clear agendas, outcomes, milestones and measures of success, connecting long-term strategy with near- and medium-term execution.
  • Identify and shape opportunities to accelerate organic and inorganic growth, strengthen competitive advantage, improve operating effectiveness or build new enterprise capabilities, bringing external market, competitive, technology and business-model perspectives to challenge assumptions and clarify trade-offs.

  • Anticipate and address the organizational, leadership, operating-model and capability implications of major initiatives, partnering across functions to drive adoption and embed required changes in how the organization operates.
  • Mobilize cross-functional teams around shared outcomes and clear accountabilities, resolving barriers, competing priorities and dependencies and adjusting course as conditions or priorities change.
  • Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to executive leaders, facilitating decisions involving competing priorities, investments, organizational interests and resource trade-offs, and communicating concise, fact-based recommendations to executive and Board-level audiences.
  • Build, lead and develop a high-performing enterprise strategy team, overseeing multiple project teams and coordinating with strategy and planning teams across the company to strengthen these capabilities organization-wide.
  • Maintain a clear view of the company’s most important strategic priorities, progress, risks and dependencies, identifying where executive intervention, additional resources or a change in approach is required.
  • Establish consistent expectations for business cases, governance, outcomes and measurement across major initiatives, partnering with Finance and business leaders to connect strategic objectives, investments and expected business outcomes.

Required Knowledge and Experiences

  • 15+ years of professional experience with progressively increasing responsibility, including significant experience in corporate strategy, a top-tier management consulting firm, or an equivalent strategic leadership role, to shape and lead the company’s most complex, ambiguous strategic priorities.

  • Strong business and financial acumen with experience developing business cases and evaluating strategic trade-offs, used to connect strategic objectives, investments and expected business outcomes.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence and lead senior executives in a complex, matrixed environment, essential for building alignment and shared accountability across businesses and functions.
  • Ability to build and lead high-performing teams while accomplishing significant work through cross-functional teams and influence, including managing multiple high-priority initiatives with significant company-wide dependencies.

Required Technical Skills

  • Exceptional problem-solving and analytical capabilities, with the ability to bring structure to complex, ambiguous challenges.

At Cencora, we are united in our responsibility to create healthier futures, and every person here is essential to us being able to deliver on that purpose. If you want to make a difference at the center of health, come join our innovative company and help us improve the lives of people and animals everywhere. Apply today!

Job Details

The Senior Director, Vision Sales leads day-to-day sales operations, coaches and develops the sales team, and ensures achievement of revenue, profitability, customer retention, and new-business targets.

This role develops long-term partnerships with strategic customers, maintains and expands existing business, and pursues new opportunities through consultative selling and coordinated sales execution.

The Senior Director uses sales, customer, and market data to shape strategy, improve team performance, strengthen customer satisfaction, and deliver profitable growth.



Primary Responsibilities:


  • Lead daily sales operations and establish clear team and individual goals aligned with organizational revenue, profitable growth, customer retention, new-business, and productivity objectives.
  • Develop and execute strategic sales and marketing plans that retain and expand existing business, generate new opportunities, and support national and regional growth priorities.
  • Partner with finance, operations, technology, marketing, and other stakeholders to evaluate, prioritize, and execute strategic initiatives and pilots, defining expected outcomes, owners, milestones, risks, investment requirements, and measures of sustained value.
  • Recruit, train, coach, and develop sales professionals while fostering a respectful, inclusive, accountable, customer-focused, and high-performing team environment.
  • Lead performance management and succession planning through regular coaching, direct and constructive feedback, performance evaluations, and development plans, and targeted capability building in consultative selling, analytics, adaptability, cross-functional leadership, and practical AI fluency.
  • Build and maintain long-term relationships with strategic customers by understanding their goals, performance trends, evolving requirements, and opportunities to deliver differentiated programs, services, and business value.
  • Serve as an escalation point for customer concerns, coordinating across functions to identify root causes, resolve issues, strengthen customer satisfaction, and prevent recurrence.
  • Establish consistent sales processes, governance, performance measures, and dashboards that provide visibility into revenue, gross profit, pipeline health, forecast accuracy, customer retention, account growth, activity, and productivity.
  • Analyze sales performance, customer behavior, pricing, market dynamics, competitive activity, and emerging industry trends to identify risks and growth opportunities and communicate actionable recommendations to leadership.
  • Diagnose operational challenges and identify system, process, and workflow enhancements by evaluating performance data, customer feedback, and sales-team needs; collaborate with cross-functional partners to prioritize solutions that improve customer experience, data visibility, productivity, and sales effectiveness.
  • Champion the responsible adoption of CRM, analytics, AI, automation, and other digital capabilities, leading stakeholder engagement, communication, training, feedback, and change-adoption activities to achieve measurable business value.
  • Manage staffing coverage, labor resources, paid-time-off schedules, vacant territories, account assignments, budget planning, pricing, and profitability decisions to maintain effective customer support and disciplined use of resources.

Education and Experience:


  • Bachelor’s degree in business administration, sales, marketing, accounting, computer science, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • A minimum of seven years of progressively responsible, directly related experience is preferred.
  • Demonstrated success in consultative sales, including at least two years in a supervisory or sales-leadership capacity.

Minimum Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:


  • Strong leadership, coaching, performance-management, team-building, and succession-planning capabilities.
  • Excellent consultative selling, relationship-building, presentation, written communication, and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong analytical and mathematical ability, including skill in interpreting sales, customer, operational, pricing, and market data.
  • Ability to lead multidisciplinary teams, collaborate across functions, and build cooperative relationships with customers and internal partners.
  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, creativity, initiative, sound judgment, and the ability to work independently.
  • Proficiency with customer relationship management platforms and other business systems used to manage sales activity and performance.

What Cencora offers

We provide compensation, benefits, and resources that enable a highly inclusive culture and support our team members’ ability to live with purpose every day. In addition to traditional offerings like medical, dental, and vision care, we also provide a comprehensive suite of benefits that focus on the physical, emotional, financial, and social aspects of wellness. This encompasses support for working families, which may include backup dependent care, adoption assistance, infertility coverage, family building support, behavioral health solutions, paid parental leave, and paid caregiver leave. jobs.excerpt: Sr.  Manager, Business Applications and Automations Join Aya Healthcare, winner of multiple Top Workplace awards!
jobs.description:
Sr. Manager, Business Applications and Automations

Join Aya Healthcare, winner of multiple Top Workplace awards!

We're looking for an experienced Director of Platform Enablement to build and lead a new team within Platform Engineering & Services. Platform Enablement exists so that a product team can get onto our cloud platform — and through its full lifecycle — without having to raise a ticket. You'll own cloud platform onboarding, tenant provisioning, environment lifecycle, developer tooling and experience, and the paved-road documentation that makes the platform usable — plus financial accountability for what tenants spend on cloud and AI, through FinOps (cloud financial operations) and TokenOps (financial operations for AI token usage). Product teams will come to you when a new product, team, or tenant needs an environment, platform access, or a lifecycle change such as an upgrade, decommission, or cost review. Your outcome is simple to state and hard to deliver: time-to-first-deploy measured in hours.

Every hour between an idea and its first deploy is an hour our clinicians and clients wait. Shrinking that — to hours, not weeks — is the job.

Who We Are:

We’re an $8+ billion, rapidly growing workforce solutions provider in the healthcare industry. We deliver tech-enabled services that help healthcare organizations meet and manage their contingent labor needs. We build and manage tech-enabled marketplaces for national and local healthcare talent and deliver contingent labor management solutions through our proprietary software platform.

At Aya, we’re obsessed with creating exceptional experiences for our clients, clinicians, and employees. In fact, we put employee satisfaction above all else. Our team members are responsible for incomparable customer experience and we know that happy employees are critical to maintaining happy clients. We foster an entrepreneurial, high-energy, low-bureaucracy culture and value innovative thinking and creative problem solving. We embrace diversity in thought and backgrounds unified by a commitment to high achievement. When you join Aya, you’ll be surrounded by teammates who care about you as an individual and leaders who will help you grow both personally and professionally.

Responsibilities:

  • Build and lead the Platform Enablement team
    • Stand up and grow a new team of platform and developer-experience engineers — hiring, performance management, career development, and a sustainable support model.
    • Run the team as a product team — with a roadmap, a backlog driven by product-team demand, user research, and measurable outcomes rather than a ticket queue.
    • Set the operating cadence — intake review, onboarding retrospectives, lifecycle and deprecation reviews, and quarterly planning against enablement metrics.
    • Build a culture of customer empathy for internal engineers, automation-first thinking, clear documentation, and disciplined ownership.
  • Make onboarding and tenant provisioning self-service
    • Own the onboarding path for every new product, team, and tenant — from first request to first production deploy — and drive time-to-first-deploy down to hours.
    • Deliver zero-ticket tenant provisioning — Azure subscriptions and landing zones, AKS namespaces and quotas, identity groups and role-based access, repositories, gateway workspaces, and baseline observability — through self-service, policy-enforced automation.
    • Build guardrails, not gates — security, cost, tagging, and compliance controls are encoded in the paved road so teams are compliant by default, with no manual approval step for standard requests.
    • Own platform access for product teams — request, grant, review, and revoke — with least privilege and an audit trail that stands up to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 review.
  • Own environment and platform lifecycle
    • Manage the full environment lifecycle — create, change, upgrade, and decommission — so every tenant has a named owner, a known state, and a clean exit.
    • Run upgrade and deprecation campaigns for tenant-facing platform versions (runtimes, cluster versions, base images, templates), with clear timelines, automated migration paths, and visible progress.
    • Retire what is no longer used — systematic decommissioning of environments, access, and resources to reduce cost, attack surface, and audit scope.
  • Own developer tooling and developer experience
    • Own developer tooling end to end — the internal developer portal (a single self-service front door for the platform), platform command-line tools, software templates, cloud and local development environments, and AI coding assistant enablement (such as GitHub Copilot and Claude Code).
    • Own developer experience (DX) as a product outcome — find and remove the friction engineers hit from first login to production, using research, usage data, and direct feedback.
    • Own the paved road — golden-path templates, starter kits, and reference architectures that make the right way the easy way.
    • Own platform documentation as a product — accurate, discoverable, versioned, and measured by whether a new team can succeed without asking for help.
    • Apply AI to enablement — AI-assisted onboarding guidance, documentation generation and maintenance, request triage, and agentic provisioning workflows, with guardrails, audit trails, and human review where risk warrants it.
    • Measure developer experience — time-to-first-deploy, self-service rate, ticket deflection, tool adoption, lifecycle currency, and developer satisfaction — and report them in plain language to leadership.
  • Own financial accountability: FinOps and TokenOps
    • Own the FinOps practice for platform tenants — making cost visible, attributable, and owned: tagging standards, showback and chargeback, budgets and alerts, right-sizing, commitment and reservation coverage, and idle-resource cleanup.
    • Own TokenOps — the financial operations of AI usage: tracking, attributing, and optimizing large language model (LLM) token consumption across teams and tools through budgets, quotas, model routing, caching, and AI gateway controls.
    • Lead tenant cost reviews with product teams and Finance — every tenant knows what it costs, why, and what to do about it — and build unit-cost views such as cost per tenant, per environment, and per AI-assisted workflow.
    • Run the team with financial acumen — own a budget, build business cases with clear return-on-investment (ROI) assumptions, weigh build-versus-buy, and give leadership forecasts it can defend.
    • Build financial fluency across engineering — coach product teams and engineers on cloud and AI pricing models, cost-aware design, and the cost impact of their choices, and keep the team learning as pricing and tooling change.
  • Clear boundaries, strong partnerships
    • Partner with Foundations who build new infrastructure primitives; Platform Enablement packages those primitives into self-service products teams can consume.
    • Partner with Delivery Engineering who own CI/CD pipelines; together you own a seamless path from a provisioned tenant to a first deploy.
    • Partner with Reliability who own production monitoring after go-live; you deliver tenants that are observable and operable from day one, with a clean go-live handoff.
    • Partner with Security Engineering, DevSecOps, and product engineering leadership to keep the paved road secure, current, and aligned with what product teams need next.

How We Will Measure Success

Within the first 12 months, the person in this role will deliver:

  • Time-to-first-deploy for a new product team or tenant measured in hours, not days or weeks.
  • Zero-ticket paths for the most common onboarding, access, and lifecycle requests.
  • Every tenant accounted for — named owner, current lifecycle state, cost visibility, and a defined decommission path.
  • Developer satisfaction with the platform and its tooling measured and trending up, quarter over quarter.
  • Cloud and AI token spend visible, attributed to an owning team, and tracking to forecast.

Qualifications:

  • 10+ years in platform engineering, cloud engineering, infrastructure, DevOps, or SRE roles, including building platforms other engineers depend on.
  • 6+ years of direct people management — hiring, performance management, and career development — including 2+ years leading managers or multiple teams.
  • Platform-as-a-product track record — built and run an internal developer platform with self-service onboarding, and can show the before-and-after metrics.
  • Deep Azure experience — 3+ years with management groups, subscriptions and landing zones, Azure Policy, role-based access, networking, and AKS. Equivalent depth in AWS or GCP will be considered.
  • Infrastructure as code and automation — Terraform or OpenTofu at scale, reusable modules, policy-as-code, and GitOps-style provisioning.
  • Multi-tenant provisioning and identity — designing tenant isolation, quotas, and least-privilege access using Entra ID, Okta, or equivalent, including access reviews and revocation.
  • Lifecycle discipline — led upgrade, deprecation, and decommissioning programs across many teams without breaking them or relying on heroics.
  • AI in engineering workflows — hands-on experience applying AI/LLM tooling to documentation, onboarding, request triage, or automated provisioning, with appropriate guardrails.
  • Developer experience ownership — owned developer tooling and experience outcomes for an engineering organization, using adoption, satisfaction, and friction data to set priorities.
  • FinOps and financial acumen — hands-on cloud financial management (tagging, showback/chargeback, budgets, optimization), budget ownership, and business cases that hold up to Finance review.
  • TokenOps awareness — understands how AI and LLM usage is priced and has tracked, attributed, or controlled AI token spend — or can show a credible plan for doing so.
  • Compliance-by-default instinct — embeds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 controls into automation and the paved road rather than bolting them on through manual review.
  • Executive-grade communication — translates platform work into business outcomes for executive, product, and engineering audiences.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related field — or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Internal developer portals — Backstage, Port, Cortex, or similar, including software templates, service catalogs, and scorecards.
  • Kubernetes multi-tenancy — AKS namespaces, resource quotas, network policies, Helm, and Argo CD or Flux.
  • GitHub Enterprise administration — Enterprise Managed Users, automated repository and team provisioning, and organization-level policy.
  • API gateway onboarding — Kong or equivalent, including self-service workspace, route, and consumer provisioning.
  • Cloudflare — DNS, Access (zero-trust network access), and Tunnel provisioning as part of tenant setup.
  • ServiceNow integration — catalog automation and audit trails for the small set of requests that still require approval.
  • FinOps certification — FinOps Certified Practitioner (FinOps Foundation) or equivalent; hands-on with Azure Cost Management and tenant-level unit economics.
  • AI gateway cost controls — Kong AI Gateway, Cloudflare AI Gateway, or similar, for token budgets, rate limits, model routing, and usage attribution.
  • Developer productivity measurement — DORA metrics (the four delivery measures from Google’s DevOps Research and Assessment program), the SPACE framework, or developer survey programs.
  • Product management practices — user research, adoption metrics, roadmapping, and running adoption and deprecation campaigns as change management.
  • Agile delivery — Scrum/Kanban delivery with Jira; comfortable operating in a quarterly planning and continuous-delivery cadence

What We Offer:

  • Free premium medical, dental, life and vision insurance
  • Generous 401(k) match
  • Aya also offers other benefits to those that are eligible and where required by applicable law, including reimbursements and discretionary bonuses
  • Aya provides paid sick leave in accordance with all applicable state, federal, and local laws. Aya’s general sick leave policy is that employees accrue one hour of paid sick leave for every 30 hours worked. However, to the extent any provisions of the statement above conflict with any applicable paid sick leave laws, the applicable paid sick leave laws are controlling
  • Celebrations! We hit our goals and reward ourselves.
  • Company-sponsored virtual events, happy hours and team-building activities are always on the horizon — plus, you get a special treat on your birthday!
  • Unlimited DTO — we believe in time off!
  • Virtual yoga, meditation or boot camp classes offered daily

Compensation: Aya reasonably anticipates the pay scale for this position to be an annual salary of $230,000 to $255,000.

The pay scale for this position may vary if applicant possesses experience outside of what Aya reasonably anticipates for this position. Bonuses are subject to the role and your manager’s discretion.

Aya is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EEO), including Disability / Vets, and welcomes all to apply. Please click herefor our EEO policy.

jobs.excerpt: WASH is a company that our customers depend on to keep them going so they can provide valuable services to their clients across USA and Canada (Coinamatic Inc.
jobs.description:
WASH is a company that our customers depend on to keep them going so they can provide valuable services to their clients across USA and Canada (Coinamatic Inc. and ParkSmart Inc). We strive to build a sense of purpose and achievement in the work we do while staying true to the DNA of our core values. We value our people and encourage the development of talented and motivated employees to support the continued performance and growth of our diverse operations. We have been the foundation of many successful careers. At our core we are an innovation driven, fast-paced team environment with a high performance culture. If you are looking for a career that will challenge and engage you, is focused on customer care and quality service, then WE are the company for you. We invite you to bring your passion and experience to our team!

WASH Commercial Laundry is seeking an experienced, results-driven Strategic Account Manager to develop, manage, and expand relationships with key national and regional property management companies, ownership groups, and strategic partners.

This position will focus on driving organic growth within existing relationships, identifying new portfolio-level opportunities, and expanding WASH's market share across the multifamily housing industry.

The Strategic Account Manager will serve as the primary relationship leader for assigned strategic accounts, working closely with WASH's field sales teams, operations, and executive leadership to deliver long-term customer value and accelerate growth.

Unlike traditional territory-based sales positions, this role focuses on building relationships with corporate decision-makers and creating opportunities across entire portfolios rather than pursuing individual property-level transactions.

Success will be measured primarily by incremental machine growth, new business opportunities, and expansion within assigned strategic accounts.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Account Development

  • Develop and execute comprehensive growth strategies for assigned national and regional property management companies and ownership groups.
  • Establish and maintain strong relationships with senior executives, regional leadership, procurement teams, and key decision-makers.
  • Identify opportunities to expand WASH's presence within existing customer portfolios, including properties currently served by competitors.
  • Develop a deep understanding of each account's portfolio, ownership structure, business priorities, and laundry service needs.
  • Build multiyear account growth plans with measurable objectives and defined opportunities.
  • Position WASH as the preferred laundry service partner across assigned customer portfolios.

Portfolio Growth and Business Development

  • Drive incremental machine growth through new property acquisitions, competitive conversions, and portfolio expansion.
  • Identify and pursue opportunities to establish preferred-provider agreements, master service agreements, and other strategic partnerships.
  • Partner with ownership and management groups to identify upcoming acquisitions, developments, and changes in property management.
  • Leverage existing customer relationships to open doors to new properties and geographic markets.
  • Develop and maintain a qualified pipeline of portfolio-level growth opportunities.
  • Coordinate with local sales teams to convert identified opportunities into signed agreements and installed machines.

Collaboration with Field Sales

  • Work collaboratively with District Sales Managers (DSMs), Regional Sales Leaders, and Account Managers to execute strategic account growth plans.
  • Create new opportunities for field sales teams through corporate and regional relationships.
  • Coordinate account strategies to ensure consistent communication and a unified customer experience.
  • Support DSMs in securing larger opportunities that require executive relationships or portfolio-level negotiations.
  • Establish clear account ownership and opportunity assignment protocols to avoid duplication or competition with field sales.
  • Ensure local sales teams remain responsible for property-level sales execution unless otherwise approved by Sales Leadership.
  • Share account intelligence, competitive insights, and growth opportunities with the appropriate sales teams.

Executive Relationship Management

  • Serve as the executive-level relationship contact for assigned strategic accounts.
  • Conduct regular business reviews with key customer stakeholders to identify growth opportunities and strengthen partnerships.
  • Collaborate with Operations and Customer Experience teams to address systemic service challenges that could impact account growth.
  • Represent WASH at industry conferences, customer meetings, and strategic business events.
  • Develop relationships that position WASH for future business opportunities and long-term partnerships.

Sales Strategy and Performance Management

  • Establish annual growth plans and measurable targets for each assigned strategic account.
  • Maintain accurate account information, growth pipelines, and opportunity tracking within CRM.
  • Provide regular forecasts and updates on signed machines, expected installations, and portfolio penetration.
  • Analyze account performance, market share, competitive positioning, and future growth potential.
  • Identify opportunities to improve customer profitability and expand WASH's overall relationship with strategic customers.
  • Partner with Sales Leadership to prioritize strategic accounts based on growth potential and business impact.

Qualifications


Required Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in strategic account management, national accounts, business development, or enterprise sales.
  • Demonstrated success managing and expanding relationships with large, complex organizations.
  • Proven ability to develop executive-level relationships and influence senior decision-makers.
  • Experience developing and executing strategic account growth plans.
  • Strong negotiation, communication, presentation, and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to work effectively across multiple departments and geographic markets.
  • Strong organizational skills and experience managing complex sales pipelines.
  • Proficiency with CRM systems and Microsoft Office applications.
  • Willingness to travel nationally as required.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in multifamily housing, commercial laundry, property management, real estate services, or related industries.
  • Established relationships with national or regional property management companies and ownership groups.
  • Experience negotiating portfolio agreements, master service agreements, or preferred-provider relationships.
  • Understanding of the multifamily housing industry's ownership and management structures.

Key Performance Indicators

Performance will be evaluated primarily on measurable growth and strategic account development, including:

  • Incremental Machine Growth: New machines signed and installed through assigned strategic account relationships.
  • Portfolio Penetration: Increased WASH market share within assigned ownership and management portfolios.
  • New Business Opportunities: Qualified growth opportunities generated and converted through strategic relationships.
  • Strategic Account Expansion: Number and value of new properties and portfolios added through existing relationships.
  • Strategic Partnerships: Development of preferred-provider agreements and portfolio-level partnerships.
  • Pipeline Development: Quality, size, and conversion of strategic account growth opportunities.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Effectiveness in generating opportunities and supporting successful execution by field sales teams.

Role Alignment and Sales Ownership

The Strategic Account Manager is intended to complement, not replace, WASH's existing field sales organization. The primary responsibility of this position is to develop relationships and generate growth opportunities at the corporate, ownership, and portfolio levels.


District Sales Managers will continue to own local property-level sales activities, including proposals, negotiations, and contract execution, unless otherwise directed by Sales Leadership.

Clear opportunity ownership and compensation crediting guidelines will be established to encourage collaboration and ensure that strategic account development supports the success of the broader sales organization.


What Success Looks Like

A successful Strategic Account Manager will:

  • Build strong executive relationships with WASH's most important strategic customers.
  • Create a consistent pipeline of incremental growth opportunities across assigned portfolios.
  • Increase WASH's share of business within major property management companies and ownership groups.
  • Generate new opportunities for DSMs and regional sales teams.
  • Establish WASH as a preferred laundry partner for major multifamily housing organizations.
  • Deliver measurable, sustainable machine growth and long-term value for WASH.

We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable federal, state, and local laws.

About Matrix Adhesives

Founded in 2021, Matrix Adhesives Group is a growth-driven company committed to delivering high-performance bonding and sealing solutions across diverse industries. We bring together some of the most trusted and innovative brands in the adhesives and sealants market - each with a proven legacy of quality, performance, and reliability.

Our portfolio includes industry-leading names–each contributing unique expertise and capabilities to meet the evolving needs of our customers. Through our brands, we offer a comprehensive range of products engineered for construction, industrial, commercial, and specialty applications.

At the core of our business is a relentless focus on operational excellence, customer partnership, and cutting-edge research and development. We don’t just supply adhesives. We help build stronger, safer, and more efficient systems for the future.

Matrix Adhesives Group is more than a supplier. We are your collaborative partner backed by a powerhouse of leading brands - committed to performance, innovation, and long-term value.

For more information visit .

About the Role

The Technical Service Manager - Building & Construction owns the front-line technical service experience for both distribution partners and end-use customers, as well as the sales organization, with particular emphasis on customer issue intake, field investigation, product-quality support, application troubleshooting and documented resolution. The role serves as the technical liaison among customers, Sales, Customer Service, Quality, Manufacturing, Laboratory and Product Development. It leads technical field support and training, coordinates testing and root-cause investigations, and actively supports new product development with application expertise and testing, and translates customer feedback and evolving market/substrate trends into actionable product and process improvements. The position is accountable for complete technical communication and follow-through; it does not replace the formal decision authority of Quality, Regulatory or R&D.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary technical contact for customers and distributors, owning issue intake, investigation and documented resolution.
  • Support Quality-led complaint, root-cause and CAPA investigations with field evidence, lot traceability and testing. Quality keeps formal decision authority.
  • Follow complaint and nonconformance procedures, escalate safety, regulatory, major-account and recurring issues promptly, and keep customer recommendations within approved product claims.
  • Identify recurring defects and complaint trends, and distinguish manufacturing quality concerns from application and process variables.
  • Run application evaluations, customer trials, demonstrations and competitive conversions with clear acceptance criteria.
  • Support new product development with application requirements, substrate guidance and validation testing, and monitor market, substrate and regulatory changes.
  • Identify B&C applications and cross-selling opportunities, resolve technical barriers and pass qualified leads to Sales. Sales owns pricing and revenue.
  • Prioritize technical projects with Sales based on customer impact and business priorities, and engage key customers and distributors proactively, before issues escalate.
  • Train internal sales teams, distributors and end users on safe product use and on selling Matrix products.
  • Produce technical reports, guides and bulletins, log activity in Salesforce, and capture customer feedback for Sales, Quality, Marketing, Product Management and R&D.
  • Coordinate across functions, join continuous-improvement efforts and follow safety requirements.
  • Own approved industry association relationships and present technical education to the industry.
  • Travel up to 50%

Critical Competencies

  • Technical and application expertise: Knowledge of adhesives, sealants, coatings and B&C applications, including substrate compatibility and troubleshooting.
  • Investigation and root-cause analysis: Structured problem solving and evidence-based conclusions, including separating manufacturing quality issues from application variables.
  • Testing and quality systems: ASTM and approved test methods, lot traceability, complaint and nonconformance SOPs, and CAPA, with an understanding that Quality owns formal decisions.
  • Customer ownership and responsiveness: Thorough issue intake, prompt follow-up, and driving each case to documented closure.
  • Technical communication and training: Clear reports, guides and bulletins, and training on safe product use and on how to sell Matrix products.
  • Cross-functional collaboration and prioritization: Working across Sales, Quality, Manufacturing, R&D and other teams, and prioritizing projects by customer impact and business priorities.
  • Commercial and market insight: Spotting cross-selling opportunities, qualifying leads, tracking market, substrate and regulatory changes, and building industry association relationships. Sales owns pricing and revenue.
  • Safety, compliance and documentation discipline: Following PPE, chemical handling and SDS requirements, escalating safety and regulatory issues, and keeping complete Salesforce and case records.

Education and Experience Requirements

  • Relevant technical service experience, application engineering, quality, laboratory or industrial field-support experience, preferably involving adhesives, sealants, coatings or related materials.
  • Experience investigating customer complaints, conducting or coordinating technical testing and documenting evidence-based conclusions.
  • Ability to communicate technical information clearly to customers and internal functions; strong follow-up, organization and customer service skills.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office; ability to maintain complete CRM and case records; willingness to travel to customer, distributor and company locations.
  • Experience supporting B&C commercial opportunities through application trials, competitive conversions and distributor/end-user training.

Equal Employment Opportunity

We are an equal opportunity employer and consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the application and employment process.

jobs.title: Cloud Engineer - Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC)
jobs.excerpt: Peraton Overview Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy.
jobs.description:
Peraton Overview

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees do the can’t be done by solving the most daunting challenges facing our customers. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking a Cloud Engineer specializing in Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) to help modernize how it manages audit, risk, and compliance. This person will help move from manual evidence collection to a cloud-engineered, continuously monitored program. This senior role owns the transformation end-to-end: the audit and assessment calendar, System Security Plan and control documentation, continuity and privacy deliverables, and compliance reporting, all rebuilt on automated pipelines this role designs and builds directly.

Work Location: Remote

Shift Schedule: 8am – 5pm Eastern Standard Time (EST)

What you will do:

Audit & Assessment Leadership

  • Own the organization's full audit and assessment calendar, ongoing/continuous control assessments, financial and IT-financial audits, internal controls testing, and security compliance audits (e.g., SOC 1 Type II). Serving as the primary point of contact for external auditors and assessors.
  • Lead recurring meetings and working sessions with the client, auditors, and assessors across the audit lifecycle: kickoffs, evidence walkthroughs, interviews, findings reviews, and status updates. Represents the organization’s control environment directly to external stakeholders.
  • Provide audit support across the full assessment portfolio, including penetration testing, red/purple/white team exercises, and periodic CISA high-value-asset assessments, incorporating all findings into the risk register and remediation lifecycle.
  • Support new system authorization (ATO) and periodic reauthorization efforts, coordinating required documentation and evidence on a recurring cycle.

Security Documentation & Control Ownership

  • Own ongoing maintenance of the System Security Plan (SSP): control implementation updates, system and technical descriptions, and review of inherited/tailored controls against the NIST 800-53 baseline. Validating control descriptions against the actual cloud architecture and configuration, not just the paper record.
  • Lead the annual review and executive sign-off cycle for core security documentation and review the organization's control catalog for accuracy against how the environment is built and configured.

Continuity & Resilience Planning

  • Own the annual review, update, and test cycle for business continuity and resilience documentation: business impact analysis, contingency plans, disaster recovery plans, and incident response plans. Grounded in the actual failover, backup, and recovery architecture of the cloud environment, not generic templates.

Privacy

  • Lead recurring privacy impact/threshold assessments in coordination with the privacy function, including technical review of how architecture handles the data in scope.

Metrics, Reporting & Automation

  • Own recurring compliance reporting deliverables: inventory reports, compliance scorecards, SLA and audit-performance metrics, progress reports, and build the automation that generates them directly from the cloud environment (native services, APIs, infrastructure-as-code state) rather than manual collection.
  • Design, build, and maintain automated evidence-collection and continuous-monitoring pipelines using native cloud services and scripting/IaC, reducing manual, screenshot-based collection across the full audit and reporting calendar above.
  • Identify the highest-value recurring manual processes across audit, documentation, and reporting work, and personally build the automation to address them. This role is expected to build, not just spec and hand off.

Governance & Stakeholder Coordination

  • Maintain governance documents that codify the organization's security and audit-support processes.
  • Serve as the point of contact for ad hoc security and privacy inquiries and impact-analysis requests from system and business owners.
  • Lead recurring coordination meetings with system owners, risk management, and compliance stakeholders to maintain shared visibility into audit status, findings, and remediation.

Skills:

  • Infrastructure depth. Hands-on experience with the organization's full technical environment: cloud (AWS), networking, databases, and midrange software (OS, VDI, Security, and administrative tool stack. Focus is to build in and extract evidence.
  • Infrastructure as Code. Able to read, write, and modify IaC (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation) to validate infrastructure configurations, and to build policy as code compliance checks into the pipeline.
  • Automation & scripting. Builds working automation (in any language — Python, Bash, PowerShell) for evidence collection, inventory reporting, and continuous monitoring; this is a hands-on build responsibility across this role's full reporting and audit workload, not an occasional task.
  • Security tooling & automation. Able to pull compliance-relevant data and build automated evidence collection from the organization’s security tool stack (e.g., SIEM, firewalls, EDR, centralized logging), not limited to cloud-native services. Capable of managing Cloud Native Application Protection Platforms (Wiz, Prisma Cloud) for enterprise “code to runtime” security with automated remediation.
  • Networking fundamentals. Understands network architecture, segmentation, and access boundaries to assess whether a control claim about network security is true in the environment. Including cloud platform's native compliance, logging, and monitoring services (e.g., AWS Config, Security Hub, CloudTrail, Audit Manager) as the primary evidence source, replacing manual collection.
  • GRC platform fluency. Administers and configure GRC/compliance automation tooling to consume evidence pulled from the cloud environment.
  • NIST 800-53 and control framework depth. Experience with control intent (not just control language) to tailor, inherit, and validate controls against real architecture.
  • Written and verbal communication. Translates technical implementation into audit-ready narrative for auditors and translates compliance/control requirements into terms that hold up in architecture and code.
  • Program and stakeholder management. Runs the full audit, documentation, and reporting calendar, with organizational discipline.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Must be a U.S. Citizen with the ability to obtain and maintain the required Public Trust level clearance
  • Bachelor's Degree and 8 years of experience, a Master's Degree and 6 years of experience, an Associate's Degree and 10 years of experience, or a High School diploma or equivalent and 12 years of experience
  • 6+ years of combined experience across cloud engineering and GRC/IT audit/information security compliance, with genuine hands-on depth in both
  • Demonstrated experience building or maintaining cloud infrastructure and automation (IaC, scripting, cloud-native tooling) in a production environment.
  • Experience conducting IRS Publication 1075 compliance reviews and Safeguards Assessments, including evaluating security controls, identifying compliance gaps, and recommending remediation actions.
  • Demonstrated experience serving as the primary point of contact between technical teams and external auditors or assessors, and owning security documentation (e.g., SSP) and control implementation.

People who live with cancer – those who work to prevent it, fight it, and survive it – are at the heart of every decision we make. Through clinical excellence and cutting-edge research, SCRI is redefining cancer care around the world.

Our Study Lead Feasibility Coordinator provides the operational process, data quality, and stakeholder coordination required to answer that question confidently.   • Maintain high-quality site capability data.
  • Support physician investigators and site staff.
  • Ensure consistent use of Veeva and feasibility processes.
  • Enable Study Leads to focus on strategic site selection and sponsor relationships.

In many ways, this role serves as the operational backbone of the feasibility process, turning site information into actionable intelligence that supports successful clinical trial execution.


The role acts as a key contact between:

  • Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI)
  • Strategic research sites
  • Physician investigators
  • CROs (Contract Research Organizations)
  • Pharmaceutical sponsors

Strong communication and responsiveness help build trust and can increase the likelihood that sponsors continue placing studies within the network.

    Certified Clinical Research Coordinator, Clinical Research Professional, or Clinical Research Associate highly preferred

Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI) is one of the world’s leading oncology research organizations conducting community-based clinical trials. Focused on advancing therapies for patients over the last three decades, SCRI is a leader in drug development. In 2022, SCRI formed a joint venture with former US Oncology Research to expand clinical trial access across the country. You'll build the data platform from the ground up and own it, with direct visibility to Finance leadership and a clear impact on how the firm closes its books.

Job Description

About this Role

The Senior Revenue Accountant plays a critical role in strengthening global revenue assurance across a diversified product portfolio, including SaaS subscription and usage-based models, professional services, and perpetual license offerings. This role helps ensure revenue processes are accurate, compliant, scalable, and aligned to the company’s growth objectives.

This position supports the review and approval of complex revenue arrangements, including multi-element contracts and non-standard commercial terms, to ensure full compliance with ASC 606. As a trusted business partner, the Senior Revenue Accountant works closely with Sales, Professional Services, Legal, Deal Desk, and other cross-functional teams to provide practical guidance on deal structure and the financial implications of customer contracts.

Operating in a global environment, this role partners with teams across regions to drive operational consistency, improve processes, and support predictable, profitable growth.

Main Responsibilities

  • Serve as a subject matter expert on revenue recognition and advise stakeholders on the application of ASC 606 across complex customer arrangements, contract modifications, and non-standard deal structures.
  • Review and analyze complex customer contracts to determine appropriate revenue recognition treatment and document technical accounting conclusions.
  • Own key aspects of the monthly, quarterly, and annual revenue close process, including reconciliations, revenue analytics, forecasting support, reserve calculations, flux analysis, and management reporting.
  • Partner with Sales, Deal Desk, Legal, FP&A, Customer Success, and Operations teams to ensure accurate contract setup, revenue forecasting, and financial reporting.
  • Identify revenue recognition risks, operational inefficiencies, and control gaps, and drive process improvements to enhance scalability and compliance.
  • Prepare and review revenue-related schedules and disclosures supporting internal and external financial reporting requirements.
  • Lead revenue accounting initiatives, including system implementations, process automation, ERP enhancements, and integration projects.
  • Collaborate with business and technology partners to define system requirements, evaluate impacts to accounting processes, and ensure alignment with company accounting policies.
  • Execute and coordinate user acceptance testing (UAT), validation activities, and change management efforts for new system implementations and enhancements.
  • Support internal and external audits by providing technical accounting support, maintaining SOX controls, and ensuring compliance with corporate policies and US GAAP.
  • Mentor junior team members and provide guidance on revenue accounting processes, controls, and best practices.

Desired Skills and Experience

  • 3-5 years of progressive accounting experience, including at least 2-4 years focused on revenue accounting within a SaaS, software, subscription-based, or technology company.
  • Strong understanding and practical application of ASC 606 revenue recognition guidance, including experience evaluating complex contractual arrangements and multi-element transactions.
  • Public accounting experience and/or experience at a publicly traded company strongly preferred.
  • CPA certification or progress toward CPA preferred.
  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or Business.
  • Demonstrated experience owning components of the monthly and quarterly close process with minimal supervision.
  • Advanced Excel skills, including complex formulas, data analysis, and reconciliation techniques.
  • Strong experience with NetSuite Advanced Revenue Management in a multi-entity, multi-currency environment is required.
  • Experience with RevPro, Salesforce CRM, Power BI, or similar financial systems and reporting tools preferred.
  • Experience supporting ERP, revenue system implementations, integrations, or process automation initiatives.
  • Proven ability to partner effectively across functions and influence stakeholders on accounting and process-related decisions.

jobs.excerpt: The Electronic Health Record (EHR) Specialist, will play a key role in optimizing EHR solutions that enable Aledade’s partner practices to improve patient outcomes, reduce healthcare costs, and increase efficiency.
jobs.description:
The Electronic Health Record (EHR) Specialist, will play a key role in optimizing EHR solutions that enable Aledade’s partner practices to improve patient outcomes, reduce healthcare costs, and increase efficiency.

The EHR Specialist will collaborate with practice stakeholders along with the multi-disciplinary Aledade team to identify, develop, and implement EHR solutions to support strategic ACO initiatives. Additionally, this role will facilitate the collection of practice-generated data that can be used for population-based analytics.

They will have depth of knowledge in at least one top-tier ambulatory EHR solution, have a strong understanding of practice workflow, and be able to travel periodically. The EHR Specialist must thrive in a fast-paced environment, respond well to change, and be a strong verbal and written communicator.

Primary Duties

    1. Lead EHR Optimization efforts for assigned projects:

      1. Coordinate efforts to conduct assessments of how practices are currently utilizing their EHR systems and identify areas where their systems can be optimized to support ACO initiatives.

      2. Assist practices to fully leverage their existing EHR systems or other 3rd party systems to support strategic ACO initiatives.

      3. Assist practices with implementing technology to provide point of care population health insights that work in conjunction with their EHR.

      4. Support practices with MIPS compliance.

    2. Provide EHR expertise:

      1. Identify common approaches, such as templates or customized reports that practices can use to achieve specific aims, such as Medicare Wellness Visits, Transitions of Care, Advance Care Planning, or Risk/Hierarchical Condition Categories.

      2. Identify existing or develop new educational materials that can assist practice staff in understanding how best to utilize their EHR system.

      3. Understand relevant EHR vendor system updates specifically related to population health management.

      4. Develop and support EHR-system-specific user groups composed of representatives from Aledade’s ACO practices to identify best practices and training opportunities.

      5. Provide strategic input on how EHR optimization can support ACO initiatives.

    3. Facilitate data exchange:

      1. Assist practices in ensuring data is properly captured in their EHR systems in order to accurately generate quality measure and other reporting.

      2. Ensure practices are able to share practice-generated data with Aledade.

      3. Assist with development of integrations, interfaces, and data sharing strategies for assigned practices.

    4. Project Management:

      1. Independently manage multiple projects at various stages to provide Aledade’s tools and train practice staff on patient-centric, value based workflows.

      2. Communicate project progress effectively to internal and external stakeholders.

      3. Present to audiences ranging from practice leadership/executives to front line staff, influencing adoption of best practices and materials that orient to Aledade’s service.

      4. Proficiently deliver detailed but concise training content on complex material to multiple client stakeholders.

Minimum Qualifications

  • A Bachelor’s degree is required. Significant and relevant work experience in lieu of educational requirements may be accepted.

  • 4-6 years experience working as a client-facing project lead in the healthcare industry (i.e., ambulatory practice, EHR vendor, health plan, hospital, government, management consulting) with a proven track record of creating, maintaining, and enhancing customer relationships and optimization of their EHR systems.

  • Must have previous implementation or optimization experience with top-tier ambulatory EHRs and practice management software, preferably with expertise in Epic Ambulatory, NextGen, Athena, Greenway, or eClinicalWorks products.

Preferred KSA’s

  • Relevant competencies include developing and maintaining relationships with all team members, organizational skills, project management, critical thinking, problem solving, attention to detail, and effective written and verbal communication.

  • Must be self motivated and open to learn new EHR platforms/workflows.

  • Must be results-oriented with the ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects in a fast-paced, dynamic environment while maintaining focus on key goals.

Physical Requirements

    Sitting for prolonged periods of time. Extensive use of computers and keyboard. Occasional walking and lifting may be required.

Who We Are:

Aledade PBC, a public benefit corporation, exists to empower the most transformational part of our health care landscape - independent primary care. We were founded in 2014, and since then, we've become the largest network of independent primary care in the country - helping practices, health centers and clinics deliver better care to their patients and thrive in value-based care. Additionally, by creating value-based contracts across a wide variety of health plans, we aim to flip the script on the traditional fee-for-service model. Our work strengthens continuity of care, aligns incentives and ensures primary care physicians are paid for what they do best - keeping patients healthy. If you want to help create a health care system that is good for patients, good for practices and good for society - and if you're eager to join a collaborative, inclusive and remote-first culture - you've come to the right place.

What Does This Mean for You?

At Aledade PBC, you will be part of a creative culture that is driven by a passion for tackling complex issues with respect, open-mindedness and a desire to learn. You will collaborate with team members who bring a wide range of experiences, interests, backgrounds, beliefs and achievements to their work - and who are all united by a shared passion for public health and a commitment to the Aledade mission.
In addition to time off to support work-life balance and enjoyment, we offer the following comprehensive benefits package designed for the overall well-being of our team members:
Flexible work schedules and the ability to work remotely are available for many roles
Health, dental and vision insurance paid up to 80% for employees, dependents and domestic partners
Robust time-off plan (21 days of PTO in your first year)
Two paid volunteer days and 11 paid holidays
12 weeks paid parental leave for all new parents
Six weeks paid sabbatical after six years of service
Educational Assistant Program and Clinical Employee Reimbursement Program
401(k) with up to 4% match
Stock options
And much more!
At Aledade PBC, we don’t just accept differences, we celebrate them! We strive to attract, develop and retain highly qualified individuals representing the diverse communities where we live and work. Aledade is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. Employment policies and decisions at Aledade are based on merit, qualifications, performance and business needs. All qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth or medical conditions related to pregnancy or childbirth), gender identity or expression, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, legally protected genetic information, marital status, veteran status, or sexual orientation.

jobs.description:
Join a team of proud, passionate, and caring people that together share their diverse talents and backgrounds to serve our members and grow the game of golf. Being at the PGA of America means you are supported, respected, and appreciated for your contributions.

The Director of Association Events & Strategic Sourcing leads long-range strategic sourcing, procurement, and contract negotiations for hotel accommodations, meeting venues, and food and beverage programs across all premier Championships and Association initiatives. This role oversees third-party vendor relationships, manages event budgets, and ensures financial stewardship and legal protection for major events, including the PGA Championship, Ryder Cup, Board of Directors meetings, Annual Meetings, governance meetings, executive leadership events, PGA REACH functions, and other Association initiatives. Additionally, the position drives operational excellence, establishes procurement best practices, and directs the planning and execution of executive and Association special events.


RESPONSIBILITIES (Specific areas of responsibility include but are not limited to):


Strategic Sourcing & Long-Range Planning

Lead the multi-year planning cycle, securing hotel room blocks, meeting spaces, event venues, and key supplier relationships up to three to five in advance of Championships and Association events.


Continually monitor hospitality industry trends, market compression cycles, and market fluctuations to identify risks and leverage negotiation opportunities early.


Lead destination research, hotel evaluations, venue assessments, and site inspections to identify facilities that best support the operational and strategic needs of the PGA of America.


Contractual Engagements & Financial Stewardship

Direct sourcing, RFP development, evaluation, negotiation, and execution of hotel agreements, all master service agreements, venue contracts, catering agreements, and other event related vendor contracts.


Negotiate contracts that protect the PGA of America from attrition, cancellation, force majeure while maximizing concessions, rebates and value added services.


Develop and manage multi million dollar event budgets, forecasting future costs while ensuring procurement decisions maximize return on investment and operational efficiency.


Association Event Planning & Association Event Management

Serve as the strategic lead for planning and executing Association events, including Board of Directors meetings, the Annual Meeting, PGA REACH events, executive leadership and governance meetings, officer functions, awards events, VIP receptions, and internal conferences and retreats.


Develop comprehensive event plans including timelines, logistics, staffing, transportation, décor, entertainment, audiovisual production, registration, signage, and overall guest experience.


Establish operational standards and best practices to ensure consistency across all Association events regardless of location.


Food & Beverage Strategy

Develop comprehensive food & beverage strategies supporting Association meetings, executive functions, and special events.


Collaborate with hotels, venues, caterers, and culinary partners to develop menus, banquet service plans, beverage programs, and hospitality experiences that reflect the PGA of America's standards.


Oversee banquet guarantees, menu pricing, catering negotiations, service standards, and budget performance.


Identify innovative culinary experiences that enhance executive and member engagement while maintaining financial discipline.


Vendor & Strategic Partner Management

Develop and maintain long-term relationships with preferred hotel brands, convention centers, destination marketing organizations, destination management companies, transportation providers, audiovisual firms, entertainment partners, production companies, rental suppliers, registration vendors, and other strategic event partners.


Evaluate vendor performance through measurable service standards while identifying opportunities for increased efficiencies, innovation, and cost savings.


Maintain preferred supplier programs that create long-term value for the Association.


Executive & VIP Experience

Develop a thorough understanding of the expectations of PGA Officers, Board Members, Executive Leadership, PGA REACH donors, Championship leadership, players, sponsors, international guests, and member volunteers.


Serve as the Association's hospitality advisor for executive meetings and special events, ensuring every experience reflects the professionalism and brand standards of the PGA of America.


Oversee executive accommodations, VIP logistics, transportation coordination, and personalized service strategies.


Cross-Functional Collaboration

Partner closely with Championship Directors, Finance, Legal, Marketing, Communications, Player Services, Volunteer Operations, Corporate Partnerships, Ticketing, and Executive Leadership to ensure all procurement and event strategies support organizational priorities.


Provide strategic guidance during championship planning related to Association functions and executive events conducted alongside PGA Championships and Ryder Cups.


Operational Excellence & Risk Management

Develop contingency plans for lodging, transportation, food & beverage, venue operations, and other critical event services.


Lead operational response during unexpected disruptions including weather, vendor issues, hotel challenges, transportation delays, and other event-related risks.


Continuously evaluate processes and implement improvements that increase efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance the Association event experience.


Team Leadership & Stakeholder Management

Recruit, mentor, and develop a high performing team responsible for strategic sourcing, special event planning, and Association meeting execution while fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, innovation and continuous improvement.


Develop a deep understanding of the diverse clientele, ranging from PGA Executives, Board Members, and PGA REACH donors to players, and various sponsors, tailoring housing strategies to meet their distinct expectations.


Manage housing bureaus, registration providers, destination management companies and other event partners to ensure seamless execution and exceptional service delivery.


INCLUSION:

Employees are expected to contribute to a respectful and inclusive team environment by welcoming and respecting others’ beliefs, backgrounds, identities, abilities, and individuality to help ensure a supportive and engaging experience for Association Members, partners, customers, and guests. PGA of America respects the uniqueness of each employee and offers everyone the means to find their place and thrive.


SHARED VALUES:

Embody the organization's shared values and help ensure the organization's values-based culture thrives by proactively identifying and addressing any shared values challenges and opportunities impacting you and your team. Keep Leadership aware of the pulse of the workforce; recognizing, discussing, and addressing any cultural concerns.


SUPERVISION:

This is a supervisory position responsible for the performance management and hiring of employees within the department.


FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY:

Responsible for preparation and oversight of the Department budget and for monitoring results.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

Bachelor’s degree (B.A.) or equivalent combination of education, training, and experience preferred.


Eight years of progressive leadership experience in strategic sourcing, hospitality management, corporate events, luxury hotel sales, meeting planning, or corporate procurement, with a focus on large-scale, citywide events and major sporting championships. Proven ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing teams.


Four years team management experience.


Extensive knowledge of hotel contract law, attrition clauses, food and beverage agreements, venue contracts, and complex corporate or association negotiations.


Demonstrated experience managing multimillion-dollar event budgets, analyzing financial data, forecasting long-term costs, identifying savings opportunities, and ensuring all contractual obligations are met.


Experience in developing standard operating procedures, planning templates, and negotiation guidelines to support consistent and efficient event execution.

Travel and hospitality experience required.


SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE AND ABILITIES:

Must have thorough knowledge of administrative principles and procedures with the ability to work on various projects and programs as assigned. A knowledge of the organization's functions of a business operation. Skills in planning and organizing. Ability to understand legal and contractual terminology as it pertains to event contracting. Ability to gather information, analyze data, and provide recommendations. Ability to maintain the confidentiality of sensitive information with the highest level of integrity. Must have working knowledge of Gmail, Google Drive, Google Sheets, and Google Docs. Basic fluency in artificial intelligence (AI) tools and concepts. This includes using AI to enhance business operations and drive innovation, enabling us to better serve our Members and stakeholders.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Aerodynamics Expert

Location: Global, fully remote

Job Type: Contract (~15 hours per week)

Schedule: Flexible—you can choose the hours and days you work, including weekends if desire

The work involves creating, solving, reviewing, and validating engineering tasks that can be completed through programmatic, command-line-based workflows. A representative task may require analyzing an airfoil, preparing a computational domain and mesh, defining appropriate boundary conditions, running a CFD simulation, calculating lift and drag, and determining whether the resulting flow field is numerically and physically valid.

Required Skills

  • Python

  • Aerodynamics

    What You’ll Work On

  1. Solve and validate aerodynamic and fluid-dynamics problems.

  2. Translate physical requirements into computational models and solver-ready cases.

  3. Create or modify geometries, computational domains, and meshes.

  4. Define appropriate initial conditions, boundary conditions, fluid properties, and solver settings.

  5. Run CFD and aerodynamic-analysis workflows using command-line-accessible tools.

  6. Use Python to automate preprocessing, simulation execution, parameter sweeps, postprocessing, and validation.

    Required Qualifications

  1. BSc, MSc or PhD in Aerospace Engineering, or Mechanical Engineering with an aerodynamics, fluid dynamics, or thermofluids specialization; or

  2. A BS in Aerospace or Mechanical Engineering plus at least 1–2 years of aero-specific professional or research experience.

  3. Strong understanding of fluid mechanics and applied aerodynamics.

  4. Experience formulating and executing CFD or aerodynamic analyses.

  5. Practical proficiency with Python or other coding languages.

Relevant tools: may include Python,OpenFOAM, SU2, Gmsh, FEniCSx, Elmer, CalculiX, SciPy, or similar programmatic engineering software. Experience with an equivalent CLI-accessible tool is acceptable.

Relevant Python tools: may include NumPy, SciPy, pandas, Matplotlib, Jupyter, solver APIs, mesh-processing libraries, or domain-specific scientific packages. No single library is mandatory.

Position Title

Credit Review Officer Sr

Location

Nationwide, MI 48098

Job Summary

Internal Credit Review’s (ICR’s) Senior Credit Review Officer position is a key individual contributor role providing the incumbent diverse exposure to a variety of portfolios and products in support of ICR’s coverage mission. The Senior Credit Review Officer is responsible for continuously monitoring and periodically examining lending portfolio asset quality and credit risk management practices. This includes evaluating the adequacy of a business unit’s credit risk governance framework including risk appetite, policies, procedures, and risk reports; the depth, accuracy, and timeliness of client financial and transaction structure analyses, risk rating and regulatory classification assignment, and potential impairment for a sample of individual exposures; adherence to credit policies, procedures, and underwriting guidelines; and the quality of ongoing surveillance and problem loan management activities. Senior Credit Review Officers report findings and recommendations to ICR and business unit stakeholders and, for defects requiring formal action, initiate reportable issues, monitor management’s remediation progress against said issues, and validate the adequacy of management actions to sustainably resolve the underlying defect. Senior Credit Review Officers may also lead or contribute to thematic topical examinations, special projects, or other department enhancement initiatives in furtherance of ICR’s mission. Senior Credit Review Officers regularly engage with stakeholders of various seniority levels from across the Bank, and as such, the position has an outsized influence on helping the organization maintain its strong credit risk management practices, safety and soundness.

Job Responsibilities:

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Participate in periodic examinations of portfolio asset quality and the design and operating effectiveness of credit risk management practices and controls. May lead said examinations for their assigned portfolio(s) and oversee the work of others on an exam-specific basis.
  • Conduct sample testing of individual credits for adherence to risk appetite and approval requirements, the quality of repayment sources and transaction structure, the accuracy and timeliness of risk ratings and regulatory classifications, and the adequacy of business unit credit analysis and other documentation.
  • Perform continuous monitoring of assigned portfolio(s), including analyzing portfolio data, underwriting and financial trends, and monitoring relevant market, industry and regulatory developments to identify emerging risks or trends. Maintain currency of ICR’s independent Risk Assessment for assigned portfolio(s).
  • Develop collaborative working relationships with business unit stakeholders to monitor portfolio, policy, process, organizational, and other developments, including the unit’s progress in remediating credit risk management defects.
  • Keep ICR leadership informed of material credit risk developments in assigned portfolio(s).
  • Collaborate with ICR team members to promote knowledge sharing, exchanges of best practices, and foster a positive and enriching work environment consistent with Bank values.

ADDITIONAL ACCOUNTABILITIES

  • Contribute to the execution of critical department operational processes such as annual planning, resource capacity and deployment analysis, staff skills assessments, issue tracking, Board reporting, and interactions with supervisors and external auditors.
  • Participate in special projects in support of enhancing ICR’s capabilities and achieving its objectives.
  • Consistently adheres to regulatory and compliance policies and standards linked to the job as listed and complete required compliance trainings. Accountable to maintain compliance with applicable federal, state and local laws and regulations.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Required Qualifications:

  • BA or BS degree; MBA, FRM, Credit Risk Certification, or other advanced degree or certification is a plus.
  • 10-15+ years of prior lending, portfolio management, credit risk management, regulatory supervision, or similar experience with commercial & industrial loan portfolios, including one or more of the following portfolio types: leveraged lending, sponsor finance, healthcare, technology, entertainment finance, asset-based lending, professional practices, or high net worth individual lending.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience analyzing distressed assets, evaluating potential impairment, and estimating individual loan loss provisions.
  • Large financial institution experience with an OCC or FRB-regulated bank.
  • Prior experience as a commercial lender or credit risk manager.

Job Competencies:

  • Expert credit / financial statement analysis skills, proven understanding of business and financial markets and the effects of economic conditions on a Bank’s credit portfolios.
  • Familiarity with US regulatory expectations related to maintaining safe and sound credit risk management practices.
  • Broad knowledge of corporate finance concepts and theories, industry credit practices, current financial and regulatory environments, and risk management techniques.
  • Ability to analyze portfolio trends at a macro level and identify leading / lagging indicators or other signs of changing risk levels and/or symptoms of process control breakdowns.
  • For more seasoned Credit Review Officers, some people or project management experience demonstrating a track record leading small teams on a permanent or temporary project basis.
  • Effective communication skills, both oral and written, and a high degree of professional maturity appropriate for interactions with business unit stakeholders as an ambassador for the ICR department.
  • Strong attention to detail, a dedication to quality, and enthusiasm for learning. Eagerness to remain current on Bank, market, and industry developments to keep skills current and sharp.
  • Strong organizational, problem solving, and communication skills.
  • Strong credit and loan structure analysis skills.
