jobs.description:
Who We Are

Imprint is on a mission to make every customer a regular.

You know how it feels when you walk into your favorite coffee shop and they know your name and start prepping your usual? Imprint makes it possible for the largest brands to create that experience at scale.

We bring payments, loyalty, and customer intelligence together in one platform, so brands can recognize and reward customers as individuals and keep them coming back. With the power of our technology and data, brands create financial products that their customers’ use everyday, earning more of their spend and increasing loyalty. Customers are rewarded with money and time saved, and surprised and delighted with a more unique, tailored experience.

We first proved our business in co-brand credit cards. For decades, the same few banks dominated the industry, building brands’ programs on mainframes older than the internet. We took a different approach, rebuilding the technology from the ground up. Today, Imprint has more than two million members, with partners like Shell, Kroger, H-E-B, and representing half a trillion dollars in total US consumer spend. Now, we’re growing our partnerships, bringing on more members, and expanding beyond credit cards so that brands offer more ways to pay and be rewarded to recognize their customers as individuals no matter their income or preferences.

Better yet, we’re doing it differently with a lean team of the most talented people on earth. Historically, companies scaled by adding people. Imprint is taking on our opportunity with a small team of exceptional people, with the best AI and technology dramatically amplifying what each person can accomplish. That means you’ll learn faster here than you could anywhere else. You’ll be one of the few people building an entirely new technology with the ownership and trust to shape what Imprint becomes. You’ll work alongside people who make you sharper everyday, armed with tools that turn your best ideas into reality faster than you thought possible. This is a rare chance to do the most important work of your career and to help prove that a small team can build what’s never been done before, inside industries that haven’t changed in decades.

Role Summary

As Senior Relationship Manager, you will run Imprint's day-to-day work with our two sponsor banks. Sitting in Regulatory Affairs, you will own bank deliverables for live programs: submission packages, approvals, bank testing follow-ups, recurring oversight and contractual reporting, and the standing relationship with each bank's working teams.

You will act as the single point of contact for the banks' working teams: keeping recurring obligations on schedule, tracked in one place, and delivered to the bank on time. Commercial's launch team owns the program and the partner; you own what the bank needs to review, approve and receive. Product, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Finance and Operations produce the underlying work, and you are accountable for the deadline and the delivery. This is a senior relationship manager role that runs bank work across both new launches and business as usual.

Responsibilities

  • Own day-to-day contact with both sponsor banks, including standing calls, follow-ups and ad hoc data requests; own the oversight and contractual reporting calendar for live programs so every report and SLA is delivered on time, owned, and tracked in one place

  • Run oversight materials, launch letters and post-launch follow-ups with the banks

  • Support senior leadership on the bank work they own: executive relationships with bank leadership, quarterly business reviews and escalations

  • Hold functional teams to bank deadlines: each team produces its own reports and artifacts, and you are accountable for on-time delivery to the bank

  • Improve and automate bank workflows to reduce manual work and turnaround time

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days

  • Taken over day-to-day contact and standing calls with both sponsor banks, and built trust with each bank's working teams through reliable execution and clear communication

  • Built a single tracker of every recurring oversight, contractual and SLA obligation to the banks, each with a named owner and due date

  • Delivered every bank report and data request due in the period on time

  • Run at least one new program or product submission through bank review, approval and launch follow-ups

  • Established working relationships with Commercial's launch team, Product, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Finance and Operations

  • Identified and implemented 2–3 process improvements that reduce turnaround time on bank submissions or reporting

Qualifications

Required

  • 8+ years of experience in fintech bank partnerships, sponsor bank operations, or program or project management in regulated financial services

  • Senior project manager who can run several launches and a full reporting calendar at once and keep each on schedule

  • Deep understanding of fintech and sponsor bank dynamics, bank oversight expectations and regulatory requirements

  • Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams and external partners without direct authority

  • Strong problem-solving skills: ability to identify issues, propose solutions, and execute independently

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with high emotional intelligence and stakeholder management capability

  • Highly organized and process-oriented, with a track record of improving workflows and driving operational efficiency

  • Grit, initiative, and ownership mindset—proactively driving outcomes rather than waiting for direction

Nice to Have

  • Experience with credit card issuance, co-branded card programs or lending at a fintech with active sponsor bank relationships

  • Familiarity with standard productivity tools: Google Workspace, Notion, Jira, Asana, Microsoft

  • Track record of centralizing knowledge, automating workflows, or scaling operational processes

  • Experience managing metrics-driven programs with clear success criteria and accountability

  • Experience preparing materials for bank oversight committees, business reviews or regulatory exams

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive compensation and equity

  • Medical plan options fully paid by Imprint, including coverage for your dependents

  • 100% company-paid dental and vision plan options

  • Mental health support through Spring Health, plus a confidential Employee Assistance Program

  • Healthcare navigation through Rightway, plus HSA, FSA and commuter benefits

  • Flexible paid time off

  • 20 weeks of paid parental leave for primary caregivers and 8 weeks for all new parents

  • The latest tools and technology, including AI, so you can do your best work

Imprint is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. Imprint is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Imprint welcomes talented individuals from all backgrounds who want to build the future of payments and rewards. If you are passionate about FinTech and eager to grow, let’s move the world forward, together.

Compensation Range: $180K - $220K

We are looking for a Senior SQL Developer to be a part of PROVE Partner's parent company Allira’s team (remote). We are making SQL the single source of truth for all of our data. Every report, reconciliation and financial statement will run from SQL, while Salesforce and Pulse remain our working systems and feed SQL, until better systems are identified. You will be the hands-on technical owner of the SQL platform. You will also scope the system migration across our Salesforce orgs, build integrations that write from SQL back to Salesforce and other systems, and manage the project day to day, working closely with Finance, Operations and our Salesforce team.

What you'll do

  • Scope the system migration across our Salesforce orgs: data mapping, sequencing, effort, risks and cutover approach
  • Design and build the SQL data model: staging, cleansed core tables and reporting marts
  • Build and schedule data loads from Salesforce, Pulse, the general ledger, loans and the loan ledger, and other sources
  • Rebuild our Salesforce reports in SQL, including accruals, repayments, settlements, clearing reports and weekly journal entries
  • Write tie-out logic that reconciles SQL to the general ledger on every load and every close

  • Work with our Salesforce team on data mapping and on changes that affect SQL

What you bring

  • Completed at least one project of similar scope from start to finish, such as a Salesforce-to-SQL migration that included reporting and finance close
  • Hands-on two-way integration experience: writing data from SQL to Salesforce and other systems (Salesforce APIs, Bulk API or middleware)
  • Project management skills: scoping, planning, running timelines and status, managing risks and stakeholders
  • 5+ years writing production SQL (T-SQL / SQL Server preferred): stored procedures, views, functions, indexing and query tuning
  • Experience building ETL / ELT pipelines (SSIS, Azure Data Factory, Fivetran or similar)
  • Dimensional modeling: fact and dimension tables, history tracking
  • Hands-on experience extracting and modeling Salesforce data

  • Clear communicator who can work directly with accountants and operations staff

Nice to have

  • Specialty finance, lending or asset management experience (advances, receivables, payoffs, fee accruals)
  • Credit facility, borrowing-base or static pool reporting
  • Power BI or SSRS report development
  • Salesforce administration or development experience
  • Git, CI/CD for database deployments
  • Project management certification (PMP or similar)

Why join

You'll build the data platform from the ground up and own it, with direct visibility to Finance leadership and a clear impact on how the firm closes its books.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity:

Position purpose


Lead the global Supply Chain Center of Excellence across three pillars: Planning Excellence & Governance; Analytics, Optimization & Value Improvement; and Data, Systems & Digital Enablement.


Strengthen supply chain performance by establishing consistent planning practices, delivering actionable analysis and measurable improvements, and enabling reliable data and effective planning technology. Partner with regional supply chain leaders to build capabilities and sustain improvements while regional teams retain operational supply and inventory accountability.


How you will thrive and create an impact


Planning Excellence & Governance

  • Establish global planning standards, business rules, decision rights, and exception thresholds.
  • Define planning horizons, freeze rules, and handoffs between master supply planning, site scheduling, materials planning, and regional supply planning.
  • Own S&OE/S&OP process design, calendars, review standards, and escalation methods.
  • Establish Plan for Every Part (PFEP) standards and review methods for finished goods, raw materials, and packaging.
  • Assess planning-process adoption and effectiveness, identify gaps, and lead improvements with regional owners.
  • Build planner capabilities through training, coaching, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement.

Analytics, Optimization & Value Improvement

  • Establish common KPIs, dashboards, and performance-analysis methods across regions.
  • Lead capacity scenarios and inventory modeling to support supply, working-capital, and investment decisions.
  • Develop inventory policies, safety-stock methods, and replenishment recommendations with regional teams.
  • Partner with Manufacturing and regional planning teams to improve capacity utilization, campaign planning, and planning parameters.
  • Identify and quantify value leakage, including excess inventory, expiry, write-offs, premium freight, and avoidable expediting.
  • Develop prioritized improvement initiatives with clear business cases, accountable execution owners, and milestones.
  • Track corrective actions and validate realized benefits with Finance, distinguishing recurring savings, cash release, and cost avoidance.

Data, Systems & Digital Enablement

  • Establish master-data standards, business ownership, validation controls, and data-quality remediation processes.
  • Prioritize SAP planning gaps and configuration issues and lead business resolution with IT.
  • Lead the business workstream for planning system implementation and SAP integration, including requirements, data readiness, testing, and deployment readiness.
  • Advance reporting and workflow automation to improve planning productivity and exception management.
  • Develop AI-enabled reporting, exception insights, and commentary with appropriate validation and accountable business review.
  • Lead planner training, system adoption, and post-implementation improvement.
  • Maintain a technology roadmap aligned with planning needs and measurable business outcomes.

Leadership and cross-functional alignment

  • Set a balanced CoE roadmap across the three pillars, prioritizing resources against business needs.
  • Lead and develop the CoE team with clear responsibilities and performance expectations.
  • Partner with regional supply chain leaders, Manufacturing, Sourcing, Quality, Finance, and IT to implement improvements.
  • Communicate progress, risks, benefits, and decisions required to supply chain leadership.

Measures of success


Planning excellence

  • Adoption and effectiveness of planning standards, PFEP reviews, and S&OE/S&OP processes.
  • Improved planning discipline, handoffs, and planner capability.

Analytics and improvement

  • Quality and use of analysis in business decisions.
  • Inventory and capacity improvements delivered with regional teams.
  • Reduction in value leakage and Finance-validated benefits.

Data and digital enablement

  • Planning-data accuracy and closure of critical data issues.
  • Delivery and adoption of SAP, Netstock, and automation improvements.
  • Measurable improvements in planning productivity and decision support.

What we're looking for


Required

  • Typically 10 or more years of progressive supply chain experience, including team leadership and cross-functional improvement.
  • Strong knowledge of master planning, capacity planning, inventory management, PFEP, and S&OE/S&OP.
  • Demonstrated experience establishing planning governance and delivering measurable operational improvements.
  • Proven leadership of teams and large, complex transformation programs across multiple sites or regions.
  • Strong track record leading planning-system implementations, organizational change, training, and sustained adoption.
  • Deep SAP planning expertise, including master-data governance and configuration, sufficient to guide business design and challenge technical solutions.
  • Strong analytical judgment, with experience directing BI reporting, dashboards, and optimization initiatives to improve business performance.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, establish planning governance, and deliver measurable operational and financial results.

Preferred

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • Chemicals or batch/process manufacturing experience.
  • Experience leading a global-scale CoE or planning transformation.
  • SAP and Netstock or comparable planning-platform experience.
  • ASCM/APICS certification, Lean Six Sigma qualification, or an advanced degree.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Product Communications
jobs.excerpt: OleOle is seeking a senior communications leader to own how our products, features, and experiences are explained to users across web and mobile.
jobs.description:
OleOle is seeking a senior communications leader to own how our products, features, and experiences are explained to users across web and mobile.

This is a hands-on role working directly with the Founder, product, design, and engineering teams. The responsibility is to understand what we are building—often before it is finished—and turn complex functionality into communication that is simple, clear, consistent, and easy for users to understand.

This person will own user-facing product communications across the OleOle platform, including onboarding and registration, social and content experiences, messaging and calling, live sports, invitations and rewards, wallets and payments, ticketing and commerce, AskOle, and future products as the platform expands.

The role will develop the language users encounter throughout the product: feature explanations, onboarding screens, calls to action, permissions and consent messaging, notifications, transaction messages, success and error states, help content, FAQs, new-feature introductions, and other communications required to launch and operate the platform.

A major responsibility will be identifying communication requirements before products launch. This person will work with product and design while experiences are being developed, reviewing flows from the user’s perspective and identifying where additional explanation, education, reassurance, or context is required.

The role will also establish OleOle’s product voice and communications standards so terminology and messaging remain consistent across different products and user journeys. As OleOle expands internationally, these standards must be designed to work across countries, cultures, and languages without losing clarity or meaning.

This person will also help develop the broader communications required around product launches and major releases, ensuring that what OleOle tells users outside the product is consistent with what they experience inside it.

This is not primarily a corporate PR or media-relations position. It is a product-focused communications role for someone who can become deeply involved in the products themselves and take responsibility for ensuring that users understand what OleOle is asking them to do, what they receive in return, and why each experience matters.

The objective is straightforward: OleOle may be technically complex behind the screen, but it should never feel complicated to the user.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in product communications, content design, UX content, product marketing, or a closely related consumer technology role, including significant senior-level ownership.
  • Demonstrated experience owning user-facing communications for a large-scale consumer technology product or platform.
  • Exceptional ability to understand complicated products and translate them into simple, clear language that consumers immediately understand.
  • Experience working directly with product managers, designers, engineers, and senior leadership throughout the product-development process—not simply receiving finished products to market after launch.
  • Strong experience developing product messaging across onboarding, feature education, calls to action, notifications, permissions, confirmations, errors, help content, FAQs, and other critical points throughout the customer journey.
  • Experience with one or more complex consumer product categories such as social media, messaging, fintech, payments, wallets, marketplaces, e-commerce, travel, ticketing, gaming, or AI.
  • Demonstrated experience establishing product voice, terminology, editorial standards, and communications systems that remain consistent across multiple products and teams.
  • Experience launching major consumer products or features and coordinating the communication required before, during, and after launch.
  • Strong understanding of how communication affects product adoption, activation, engagement, trust, retention, and conversion.
  • Experience communicating sensitive or high-trust experiences such as payments, financial transactions, identity verification, privacy, security, permissions, rewards, or account access.
  • Experience building communications for international products and working with localization and translation across multiple languages and cultures.
  • Excellent written English and exceptional editing skills, with the judgment to know when users need additional explanation and when fewer words create a better experience.
  • Strong product judgment and the confidence to challenge unclear product experiences rather than attempting to solve every usability problem with additional copy.
  • Comfortable operating in an early-stage, fast-moving environment where products are being designed and built simultaneously and requirements continue to evolve.
  • Highly hands-on. The successful candidate must be willing to personally write, edit, review, and establish the communications system rather than simply manage agencies, vendors, or a large communications team.

Strongly Preferred

Experience at a major global consumer technology company with sophisticated, multi-product user experiences—particularly social, messaging, payments, fintech, marketplaces, travel, commerce, or other high-frequency consumer platforms.

Experience helping a product expand internationally and maintaining a consistent product voice across markets and languages is particularly valuable.

Compensation

This role begins under OleOle’s deferred compensation model. Compensation is earned from the start under a written deferred compensation agreement and becomes payable when the company closes its funding; this is not unpaid or free work. Our current team, including the Founder, is working under the same structure. Candidates should understand that there is real risk because the timing of funding cannot be guaranteed. Following funding, the position will transition to a competitive salary plus equity and token ownership.

Solutions not problems .

  • Creative problem solver who can courageously propose and support new ideas to our organization. Not interested in best practices, lets build something better!
  • Ability to adapt. An ideal candidate will welcome the opportunity to solve a broad range of problems using a wide array of technologies.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity, shifting priorities and general growing pains of an early-stage technology company
  • An exceptional entrepreneurial judgment that fosters independence over micro-management
  • Understanding of football and international sports a huge plus

Ole Ole is located in beautiful Austin Texas, however, this role requires some travel we are privately held and rapidly growing!

OleOle is building a global social, messaging and commerce platform designed specifically for the more than three billion football fans around the world.

The platform brings together social media, short-form video, encrypted messaging and calling, live scores, real-time translation and football content within a single global ecosystem. Our goal is to connect fans across clubs, countries and languages while creating an infrastructure that extends well beyond social media.

Every OleOle user receives a persistent Wallet ID that connects their identity across the ecosystem. Over time, OleOle will integrate payments, commerce, Mini Programs, ticketing and travel, gaming, digital assets and financial services. Mini Programs will allow clubs, brands, merchants and third-party developers to build services directly within OleOle, using the platform’s identity, social and payment infrastructure.

OleOleSport, our ticketing and travel business, provides an important early commercial opportunity through tickets, VIP hospitality and travel experiences around major sporting events. As the OleOle audience grows, additional businesses are designed to scale alongside it, including Mini Programs, payments, gaming and NewZeros, our planned financial infrastructure combining exchange capabilities with a broader payments and transaction network.

We are currently a team of approximately 20 people building across backend infrastructure, social, video, messaging, AI and translation, payments, football data, product and design.

OleOle is being built around a long-term thesis: football is the world’s largest shared passion, yet its global audience remains fragmented across social networks, messaging applications, sports platforms and commerce providers. We believe there is an opportunity to bring those experiences together in one global platform and build significant businesses around the resulting network.

OleOle — Where Fans Kick Off.

jobs.excerpt: About Us Buddle was founded to address the growing demand for reliable and efficient staffing solutions across diverse industries globally.
jobs.description:
About Us

Buddle was founded to address the growing demand for reliable and efficient staffing solutions across diverse industries globally. Our mission is to seamlessly connect businesses with skilled professionals, fostering long-term partnerships that benefit both parties. At Buddle, we prioritise trust, value, and sustainability in every staffing solution we provide.

About the Role

We are looking for a hands-on and resourceful Car Rental Fleet Manager to oversee vehicle repair coordination, maintenance scheduling, mechanic assignments, and fleet inventory management.

In this role, you will receive reports of vehicle breakdowns, mechanical issues, customer complaints, and repair requests. You will be responsible for understanding the reported issues, identifying the likely repairs needed, coordinating with available mechanics, assigning repair jobs, and ensuring that repairs are completed within a reasonable timeframe.

The ideal candidate has a good understanding of vehicle mechanics, can confidently communicate repair requirements to mechanics, and is capable of managing multiple repair jobs, schedules, and inventory requirements to keep the rental fleet operational and minimise downtime.

Key Responsibilities

Vehicle Repair Assessment and Diagnosis

  • Receive and assess reports of vehicle breakdowns, mechanical problems, customer complaints, and repair requests.
  • Understand reported symptoms and identify possible mechanical faults and the repairs required.
  • Conduct initial troubleshooting to determine the likely cause of vehicle issues and the urgency of repairs.
  • Clearly explain vehicle issues, repair requirements, and priorities to assigned mechanics.
  • Determine whether a vehicle requires immediate repair, further inspection, or routine maintenance.
  • Monitor recurring mechanical problems and recommend appropriate corrective actions.

Mechanic Assignment and Coordination

  • Identify and contact available mechanics or service providers based on the type of repair, availability, location, and urgency.
  • Assign repair and maintenance jobs to appropriate mechanics.
  • Coordinate with mechanics to ensure they understand the reported issue, scope of work, and expected turnaround time.
  • Follow up with mechanics regarding repair progress, delays, and completion.
  • Maintain a network of reliable mechanics and service providers who can support different vehicle repair requirements.
  • Coordinate additional support when a repair requires specialised expertise.

Scheduling and Fleet Maintenance

  • Manage and schedule vehicle repairs, maintenance, servicing, inspections, and other fleet-related work.
  • Coordinate mechanic schedules and assign jobs based on repair priorities and availability.
  • Ensure urgent vehicle issues are attended to promptly.
  • Monitor repair timelines and follow up to ensure jobs are completed as scheduled.
  • Coordinate vehicle availability with rental bookings and operational requirements.
  • Minimise vehicle downtime by efficiently managing repair schedules and prioritising vehicles that need to return to service.

Inventory and Parts Management

  • Monitor inventory of vehicle parts, tools, supplies, and other maintenance-related materials.
  • Identify parts required for scheduled repairs and coordinate their availability before work begins.
  • Track inventory usage, stock levels, and replenishment requirements.
  • Coordinate sourcing and purchasing of parts when necessary.
  • Maintain accurate inventory records and ensure commonly used parts are available to avoid unnecessary repair delays.

Fleet Monitoring and Record Management

  • Maintain updated records of vehicle condition, repair history, maintenance schedules, and current operational status.
  • Track vehicles that are available for rental, undergoing repairs, awaiting parts, or temporarily out of service.
  • Document repair reports, mechanic assignments, parts used, repair costs, and completion dates.
  • Keep relevant stakeholders updated on vehicle status, repair progress, and expected availability.
  • Maintain organised and accurate fleet maintenance records.

Reporting and Operational Improvement

  • Provide updates on outstanding repairs, mechanic assignments, vehicle availability, and inventory requirements.
  • Monitor repair turnaround times and identify recurring delays or operational issues.
  • Identify opportunities to improve mechanic coordination, scheduling, inventory management, and repair processes.
  • Recommend practical ways to improve fleet reliability and reduce maintenance-related downtime.

Other Responsibilities

  • Make necessary process suggestions and improvements which can help the team.
  • Contributes to team effort by accomplishing related results as needed.
  • Perform other related tasks and duties that may be assigned by the client later on.

About You

You're a hands-on, resourceful, and highly organised professional with a strong understanding of vehicle mechanics, repair processes, and fleet maintenance operations. You're capable of assessing reported vehicle issues, identifying likely repairs, coordinating mechanics, and managing multiple repair jobs and schedules. You take ownership of issues from initial report through to resolution and are comfortable working independently in a fast-paced operational environment.

Essential Experience and Skills

  • 3–5 years of experience in fleet management, fleet maintenance, automotive repair, workshop operations, or a related automotive role.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Practical knowledge of vehicle mechanics, common mechanical faults, troubleshooting, and repair requirements.
  • Ability to assess vehicle breakdown reports, customer complaints, and reported symptoms to identify likely mechanical issues and determine the appropriate repairs.
  • Experience coordinating, scheduling, and assigning mechanics or automotive technicians based on repair requirements, availability, and urgency.
  • Experience managing multiple repair jobs, monitoring progress, and following up to ensure timely completion.
  • Knowledge of routine vehicle servicing, preventative maintenance, inspections, and repair scheduling.
  • Experience monitoring vehicle parts, supplies, inventory levels, and replenishment requirements.
  • Ability to communicate repair requirements clearly to mechanics, workshops, and service providers.
  • Strong organisational, prioritisation, and time management skills, particularly when handling multiple vehicles and urgent repairs.
  • Ability to maintain accurate records of vehicle repairs, maintenance history, mechanic assignments, inventory, and vehicle status.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to make sound decisions regarding repair priorities and fleet operational requirements.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently, take ownership of responsibilities, and coordinate effectively in a remote working environment.

Nice to Have

  • Experience working in a car rental, vehicle hire, transport, logistics, or automotive service business.
  • Previous experience as an automotive mechanic, workshop supervisor, service advisor, fleet maintenance coordinator, or workshop manager.
  • Experience coordinating independent mechanics, external workshops, and third-party service providers.
  • Experience sourcing automotive parts, obtaining repair quotations, and coordinating repair costs.
  • Familiarity with fleet management systems, vehicle maintenance tracking tools, or inventory management systems.
  • Knowledge of vehicle roadworthiness requirements, inspections, and maintenance compliance.
  • Experience managing or coordinating the maintenance of multiple vehicles within an active rental fleet.
  • Experience working in a remote operations environment and coordinating with geographically dispersed teams or service providers.

Director, AP Sales Enablement

College Board – AP&I

Location:

Role Type:

  • This is a full-time position

About the Team

The AP Access and Implementation team focuses on expanding the benefits of AP to more high school students by supporting schools, districts, and states in adopting and sustaining AP courses. The team works across AP Program, AP Outreach, State and District Partnerships, Engagement and Reach, Research, and other divisions to help schools understand the value of AP and the practical pathways for implementation.

About the Opportunity

The Director, AP Sales Enablement, will lead the strategy, output, and outcomes for how effectively AP products, updates, and value propositions are positioned and executed in the field to drive new business and state and district growth. 

This role is responsible for ensuring that go-to-market strategy translates into clear, differentiated materials, strong sales team readiness, and high-quality execution across state and district sales efforts. This includes not only developing sales materials and positioning, but actively enabling and coaching sales teams to deliver effective, consistent, and compelling engagements. 

This role goes beyond content development. The Director is responsible for driving the AP sales enablement strategy and requires hands-on partnership with sales teams, including leading trainings, supporting high-stakes engagements, and working directly with teams to improve how the AP is positioned in competitive environments. Reporting to the Senior Director, AP Growth, this individual is a key driver of AP growth, partnering closely with field teams and AP leadership to ensure go-to-market strategy translates into successful outcomes in the field. 

Success in this role is defined not by the volume of materials produced, but by measurable improvements in execution and the quality of customer conversations. 

In this role, you will:

Lead Program Sales Enablement Strategy and Outcomes (35%) 

  • Recommend improvements to the end-to-end program sales enablement strategy for AP go-to-market efforts, ensuring sales teams are equipped to drive awareness, consideration, and decision-making 
  • Translate product updates, program strategy, and competitive positioning into clear, differentiated materials that improves sales effectiveness
  • Drive alignment across AP and field teams as a key leader in the cross-divisional AP go-to-market process, including ownership of sales cycle collateral development and updates, as well as the SDP briefing process, to ensure consistent and compelling AP positioning 
  • Be accountable for field and sales readiness at key moments, including major launches, state pursuits, and district growth initiatives 

 

Drive Sales Team Readiness, Training, and Execution (30%) 

  • Lead end-to-end program enablement of SDP and inside sales teams, ensuring they can confidently and effectively position the AP in customer conversations 
  • Design and deliver AP training experiences, including ownership of SDP briefings, live sessions, small group workshops, and one-on-one coaching with sales teams 
  • Partner directly with sales teams to refine materials and messaging, strengthen delivery, and improve effectiveness in real customer engagements 
  • Travel to support regional sales teams, major sales opportunities, and high-stakes sales engagements as needed 
  • Identify and close gaps in execution using sales team feedback, performance signals, and win/loss insights 
  • Ensure enablement efforts result in measurable improvements in sales confidence, consistency, and effectiveness 

 

Lead Collateral, Playbooks, and Pursuit Support (20%) 

  • Lead the development and maintenance of core sales assets, including pitch decks, playbooks, competitive positioning guides, and leave-behind materials 
  • Translate program strategy into clear, practical tools that sales teams can use effectively in live customer conversations 
  • Support development of state and district pursuit materials, including positioning, themes, and RFP narratives 
  • Ensure all materials are current, consistent, and tightly aligned to go-to-market strategy and sales execution needs 

 

Drive High-Stakes Engagements and Improve Sales Performance (15%) 

  • Partner with sales teams and AP leadership to directly support high-stakes state and district engagements, including presentations, strategy sessions, and key customer interactions 
  • Support AP representation at conferences and external events, serving as a credible resource and strengthening market presence and influence 
  • Build bench strength across AP by enabling more teacher consultants to effectively represent AP externally, reducing reliance on a small number of program leaders 
  • Use win/loss insights, field feedback, and performance signals to identify gaps in positioning and execution 
  • Continuously refine messaging, collateral, and enablement strategies to improve sales cycle effectiveness and the quality of customer conversations 

About You

Exceptional candidates can effectively speak to:

  • At least 8 years of relevant professional experience in education, program strategy, practitioner network management, consulting, or a related field.
  • Experience teaching AP is strongly preferred.
  • Experience coaching or supervising AP teachers, preferably as an assistant principal or district administrator.
  • Strong working knowledge of AP implementation, including scheduling, staffing, student recruitment, teacher readiness, course sequencing, and adoption barriers.
  • Experience identifying, training, coaching, managing, or evaluating educators, consultants, ambassadors, fellows, champions, or practitioner networks.
  • Ability to use data, surveys, evaluations, and feedback to assess quality, improve execution, and inform talent decisions.
  • Experience advising senior leaders and translating evidence into talent, investment, and operating model recommendations.
  • Experience setting strategy and making portfolio, capacity, quality, or resource allocation decisions for a distributed network.
  • Ability to conduct independent analysis, identify strategic options, and recommend which courses, audiences, and engagement models should receive investment.
  • Ability to travel up to 40% for national meetings, major conferences, and in person events, including AP Annual Conference.
  • Strong communication, facilitation, presentation, project management, and cross functional coordination skills.
  • Strong judgment, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple workstreams in a matrixed organization.
  • Commitment to expanding student access to AP and supporting successful AP course implementation.

Preferred qualifications include:

  • Experience supporting instructional sales, adoption communications, or school implementation initiatives.
  • Familiarity with AP Program priorities, AP expansion strategies, and school priority framing.
  • Experience using research, market insights, program data, and field feedback to improve messaging and execution.
  • Experience developing scalable systems, templates, and processes for distributed teams.

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.

A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $80,000–$130,000.
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

jobs.description:
At Qualtrics, we create software the world’s best brands use to deliver exceptional frontline experiences, build high-performing teams, and design products people love. But we are more than a platform—we are the creators and stewards of the Experience Management category serving over 18K clients globally. Building a category takes grit, determination, and a disdain for convention—but most of all it requires close-knit, high-functioning teams with an unwavering dedication to serving our customers.

When you join one of our teams, you’ll be part of a nimble group that’s empowered to set aggressive goals and move fast to achieve them. Strategic risks are encouraged and complex problems are solved together, by passing the mic and iterating until the best solution comes to light. You won’t have to look to find growth opportunities—ready or not, they’ll find you. From retail to government to healthcare, we’re on a mission to bring humanity, connection, and empathy back to business. Join over 5,000 people across the globe who think that’s work worth doing.

Solutions Consultant - Senior Principal, NA ENT

Why We Have This Role

Our pre-sales team helps some of the largest organizations in the world find and close experience gaps with the Qualtrics XM Data & AI Platform, which combines experience management (XM) data with artificial intelligence (AI) to predict what comes next and act on it.

As a Solutions Consultant in our Financial Services and Insurance (FSI) business, you will partner with Sales Teams on opportunities across banking, insurance, wealth and asset management, and payments. You bring the product skills to show what the platform can do and the strategic perspective to help business leaders decide what to do with it. In an industry shaped by regulation, rising customer expectations, digital disruption and retention pressure, you will connect XM and AI to outcomes FSI leaders care about, such as customer loyalty, advisor and agent effectiveness, claims and servicing quality, and operational risk.

While most of your efforts will be focused in the pre-sales environment, some additional cross-functional initiatives may include input in product direction, content generation, contributing to analyst reports/relationships and attending marketing events.

You will report to a Solution Consulting Manager.

How You’ll Find Success

  • Earning trust with Account Executives as their go-to partner on deal strategy and execution in FSI accounts.
  • Becoming a trusted advisor to customer business and technology leaders, helping them build their XM vision and a roadmap toward the art of the possible.
  • Building and delivering compelling product demonstrations that show the value of Qualtrics in the context of FSI use cases and workflows.
  • Winning the technical decision and the business case on enterprise deals with multiple stakeholders.
  • Contributing to team outcomes, including win rate, pipeline, net new annual recurring revenue (ARR) and customer satisfaction.
  • Sharing what works and helping your peers grow.

How You’ll Grow

  • Learn the full XM platform, including customer experience, employee experience and market research, and the AI capabilities that connect them.
  • Build deep FSI expertise across banking, insurance, wealth management and payments, including the regulatory, security and data considerations that shape buying decisions.
  • Deepen your expertise in AI and data and shape how FSI customers apply them to business outcomes.
  • Build influence with Product and Marketing by bringing field insight into product direction and go-to-market strategy.
  • Grow your career through a structured promotion process, career action planning with your manager, and internal mobility (Qmobility).
  • As we build an AI-first company and change the market for Experience Management, you will be at the cutting edge of this transformation in enterprise software.

Things You’ll Do

  • Partner with account executives on deal strategy and account planning for FSI opportunities.
  • Contribute to discovery by owning technical discovery, uncovering business challenges and tying them to measurable outcomes.
  • Design, build and deliver tailored use case solutions and demonstrations, including FSI scenarios such as digital banking journeys, contact center and voice of the customer programs, claims and policy experiences, advisor and agent feedback, and employee engagement.
  • Build business cases and value stories that translate product capabilities into value drivers for FSI buyers, connecting XM and AI to revenue, cost and risk.
  • Facilitate executive briefings and workshops that help customers shape their XM vision and roadmap.
  • Advise customers on XM program design and governance, including use-case prioritization, data sources, closed-loop action, a phased maturity roadmap, program ownership, operating model and regulatory considerations specific to financial services.
  • Answer technical questions on architecture, integrations, APIs, security, privacy and data, including the questions FSI security and compliance teams ask.
  • Position Qualtrics against competitors on both product strengths and business value.
  • Support expansion with existing FSI customers by identifying new use cases across business lines and XM areas, including customer, employee and market research.
  • Share customer and field feedback with Product Management, Marketing and Engineering, contribute to content, events and enablement, and stay current on FSI industry trends, regulation and competitor moves.

Required Qualifications

  • 5 or more years in pre-sales, solutions engineering, solution architecture, consulting or another customer-facing technical or strategic role at a business-to-business (B2B) software as a service (SaaS) company, or as a practitioner leading customer, employee or research programs.
  • Experience supporting sales cycles both strategically and technically with director, vice president and C-level buyers.
  • Strong technical aptitude and the drive to configure, build and deliver software demonstrations tailored to a customer's needs.
  • Ability to explain and resolve common technical aspects of SaaS software, including security, API protocols and integrations, and SLAs.
  • Experience building a business case or value story that ties a solution to measurable outcomes.
  • Working understanding of AI and data-driven solutions.
  • Excellent written and spoken communication, including presenting to executives.
  • Ability to explain industry trends and complex concepts, including regulatory and market shifts in financial services, clearly to business audiences who are not subject matter experts.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and the initiative to pivot as needs change.
  • Undergraduate degree in business, finance, economics, psychology, computer science, information systems, a quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Legally authorized to work in the United States.
  • Ability to travel up to 25%.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience selling to or working with financial services or insurance organizations, such as banks, credit unions, insurers, wealth and asset managers, or payments companies.
  • Familiarity with FSI regulatory, security and data privacy expectations and how they affect software buying decisions.
  • Experience with Customer or Employee Experience software or programs, including contact centers and voice of the customer.
  • Experience consulting on the design and implementation of Employee or Customer Experience Management (XM) programs, or working with enterprise CX, EX or research teams at large organizations.
  • Hands-on experience with AI and large language models in a customer-facing setting, including using AI tools to improve how you sell and go to market.
  • Knowledge of survey design, change management, or quantitative and qualitative data analysis.
  • Experience reading and debugging HTML, CSS, JavaScript or SQL, with the support of AI tools

What You Should Know About This Team

  • We play a critical role in the commercial engine, driving innovation and market penetration through direct work with customer decision makers and scaling our expertise across the field.
  • Our team values initiative and independence. Everyone is encouraged to think ahead, anticipate potential issues and solve them proactively.
  • We are known for our collaborative spirit, a strong desire to learn and, most importantly, a commitment to our customers’ success. We help Sales and Qualtrics hit their targets by building customer confidence and demonstrating the value of our technology. We are comfortable in a fast-changing environment, and creativity is often our best tool.

Our Team’s Favorite Perks and Benefits

  • Pension plan match
  • We offer private dental and health insurance
  • Wellness reimbursement - up to the value of $300 per quarter can be reimbursed for a variety of wellness activities

The Qualtrics Hybrid Work Model: While this role is exempt from working in office, our hybrid work model remains elegantly simple for the rest of the company: we all gather in the office three days a week; Mondays and Thursdays, plus one day selected by your organizational leader. These purposeful in-person days in thoughtfully designed offices help us do our best work and harness the power of collaboration and innovation. jobs.excerpt: Are you passionate about being part of a team at a Fortune 100 company with nearly $70 billion in annual sales that delivers extraordinary care to help individuals and businesses prepare for and protect their future?
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about being part of a team at a Fortune 100 company with nearly $70 billion in annual sales that delivers extraordinary care to help individuals and businesses prepare for and protect their future? If so, then Nationwide Financial could be the place for you! At Nationwide®, “on your side” goes beyond just words. Our customers and partners are at the center of everything we do and we’re looking for associates who are passionate about delivering extraordinary care.

Join Nationwide’s Life Underwriting team as a Specialist supporting our Hantz Financial partnership. In this role, you’ll apply your life underwriting experience and critical-thinking skills to evaluate cases, weigh available information, and make sound, well-supported risk decisions. You’ll partner with underwriting colleagues and business contacts to deliver responsive service in a relationship-focused business with repeat customers and complex coverage needs, including survivorship cases. Success in this role calls for strong judgment, attention to service expectations, and the ability to manage your work independently from review through decision.


This role is open to fully remote work.


This role does not qualify for employer sponsored work authorization. Nationwide does not participate in the STEM OPT extension program.


Job Description Summary

Our underwriters work hard to provide the exceptional customer experience for which Nationwide is known. Actively engaging with our firms and financial professionals to get to know their clients and their needs builds our understanding of the market, what is needed to win business and put our best offer out first.

If you thrive working autonomously, making decisions on a variety of impactful issues and continuing to learn and adapt to grow, we want to know more about you!

As a Senior Life Underwriting Specialist, you'll analyze, select and classify applications for life insurance of a more complex nature according to established underwriting policies, practices and standards. You'll coordinate life insurance selection standards according to underwriting practices and procedures to achieve satisfactory mortality and morbidity experience and acceptable administrative results. We'll count on you to use independent judgment based on your underwriting authority and company underwriting standards. You will also likely serve as a referral point for less experienced underwriters and will often have cross distributional experience. You may also represent your distribution on underwriting related projects.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities:

  • Receives, evaluates and underwrites, on a medical or non-medical basis more complex applications for life insurance up to their maximum handling limit as approved by the Chief Underwriter. Protects the confidentiality of documentation and information acquired throughout the underwriting process. Works independently, but engages referral points, mentors and staff underwriting and medical staff for complex issues and cases.

  • Maintains in-depth knowledge of manuals, underwriting materials, rules, regulations, procedures medical factors and practices impacting mortality and morbidity underwriting. Maintains proven understanding of all underwriting administrative systems to conduct business and provides outstanding service to all internal and external customers and field partners.

  • Evaluates and accesses applications requiring additional evidence of insurability. Determines the need for and authorizes the ordering of, underwriting requirements to include, but not limited to, medical examinations, blood profiles, home office specimens, attending physician reports, inspection reports, client direct interviews, and other essential information.

  • Develops a strong understanding of the accelerated underwriting process and can apply risk-based decision-making skills to determine the appropriate requirements needed to provide protective value as well as determining appropriate risk class. This may include but not limited to, making fluid-less underwriting decisions as well as the utilization of alternative sources of medical information while maintaining appropriate tolerance for accepting risk.

  • Consults with other underwriters and accepts referred cases when designated. Suggests innovative solutions, motivates team performance and facilitates open communication to achieve results.

  • Evaluates, appraises and quantifies data derived from personal or business financial information and establishes insurable interest in keeping with the principle of indemnification. Assists with training other team members in this area

  • Reaches terms on and coordinates both automatic and facultative reinsurance within the contractual terms and conditions of Nationwide's various reinsurance treaties and product and market practices.

  • Meets and presents with field partners as needed. Acquires input and feedback during these visits to build a better understanding of partner needs and expectations.

  • Determines eligibility for temporary insurance and authorizes disbursement of policy refunds if the Temporary Insurance Agreement (TIA)is not eligible. Also authorizes reimbursement for medical records or other fees associated with requirements needed to confirm evidence of insurability.

  • Interprets electrocardiogram tracings received as evidence for life insurance applications. Consults with Medical Director on cases where physician input is required.

  • Consults with Chief Underwriter, Staff Underwriting, Underwriting Consultants, Senior Underwriters and the Medical Director as the need arises.

  • Supports and assists in meeting goals and objectives for varying territories, special agent programs and contests.

  • Resolves challenges with effective solutions while maintaining focus on improving time service, quality of application submissions and underwriting quality

  • Handling up to $5,000,000 for life, up to $750,000 sign off for morbidity underwriting, and ability to sign off on exceptions for Intelligent Underwriting.

May perform other responsibilities as assigned.

Reporting Relationships: Reports to Underwriting Manager or Director

Typical Skills and Experiences:

Education: Undergraduate studies in medical related discipline, marketing, insurance, risk management, economics, finance or business management preferred.

License/Certification/Designation: LOMA Level 1 Certificate (LOMA 280, LOMA 290) preferred. Participation in, or attainment of, professional/technical studies or designation such as ALMI (ALU Level 1 Cert, ALU 201, 202, LOMA 320, 335).

Experience: Five years of life underwriting experience

Knowledge, Abilities and Skills: Proven foundation for basic financial underwriting. Ability to evaluate the life financial supplement, understand more sophisticated beneficiary situations, e.g., buy/sell agreements, beneficiaries other than immediate family, foreign risks. In-depth knowledge of anatomy, physiology, pathology and non-medical risks. For investment life, proven knowledge of independent distribution systems.

Relationships: Very comfortable negotiating offers and calling out on offers that are other than applied for to explain reasons to the advisor or sales leader.

jobs.excerpt: Circle (NYSE: CRCL) is one of the world’s leading internet financial platform companies, building the foundation of a more open, global economy through digital assets, payment applications, and programmable blockchain infrastructure.
jobs.description:
Circle (NYSE: CRCL) is one of the world’s leading internet financial platform companies, building the foundation of a more open, global economy through digital assets, payment applications, and programmable blockchain infrastructure. Circle’s platform includes the world’s largest regulated stablecoin network anchored by USDC, Circle Payments Network for global money movement, and Arc, an enterprise-grade blockchain designed to become the Economic OS for the internet. Enterprises, financial institutions, and developers use Circle to power trusted, internet-scale financial innovation. Learn more at .

What you’ll be part of:

Circle is committed to visibility and stability in everything we do. As we grow as an organization, we're expanding into some of the world's strongest jurisdictions. Speed and efficiency are motivators for our success and our employees live by our company values: High Integrity, Future Forward, Multistakeholder, Mindful, and Driven by Excellence. We have built a flexible work environment where new ideas are encouraged and everyone is a stakeholder.


What you'll be responsible for:


As Business Development Manager, DeFi Liquidity, you will lead the design, execution, and optimization of liquidity programs supporting trading activity on Arc, Circle's blockchain network for institutional-grade on-chain financial activity. Working closely with colleagues responsible for external venue partnerships and internal trading products, you will ensure that both internal and external venues have the liquidity infrastructure and participation needed to support effective trading. You will leverage existing relationships with DeFi liquidity providers, market makers, and trading firms while developing new partnerships, building data-driven liquidity strategies, and managing programs from initial structuring through deployment and ongoing performance optimization. Your work will help establish sustainable liquidity, improve trading execution, and support the growth of Arc's on-chain trading ecosystem.


What you'll work on:


  • Design and execute liquidity programs for internal and external Arc trading venues, aligning incentives with venue structure and trading requirements.
  • Develop and expand relationships with DeFi liquidity providers, market makers, and trading firms to support liquidity deployment across Arc.
  • Build financial and liquidity models evaluating TVL requirements, fee structures, incentive economics, slippage, and expected trading activity.
  • Partner with Product and Venue GTM teams to inform trading venue design, liquidity architecture, fee tiers, and integration strategies.
  • Lead liquidity partnership negotiations, including program proposals, commercial terms, capital commitments, and deployment coordination.
  • Monitor liquidity performance, trading volume, capital efficiency, and incentive effectiveness to identify opportunities for optimization.
  • Translate DeFi market structure developments and liquidity provider feedback into actionable recommendations that strengthen Arc's trading ecosystem.

What you'll bring to Circle:


Core Requirements

  • 7+ years of relevant professional experience, including substantial hands-on experience in crypto, DeFi trading, or liquidity provision.
  • Direct experience designing, executing, or managing on-chain liquidity programs within a DeFi protocol, market maker, or trading firm.
  • Strong knowledge of DeFi market structure, including AMMs, concentrated liquidity, proprietary AMMs, liquidity provisioning models, and aggregator routing.
  • Demonstrated ability to model liquidity requirements, incentive economics, fee optimization, and slippage to support data-driven commercial decisions.
  • Established relationships with DeFi liquidity providers, market makers, and trading desks, with experience developing and managing commercial partnerships.
  • Experience negotiating liquidity arrangements and managing the commercial lifecycle from initial engagement through deployment and ongoing optimization.
  • Ability to collaborate with Product and Engineering teams, evaluate technical specifications, and translate liquidity requirements into actionable product recommendations.

Preferred Requirements

  • Experience deploying liquidity across multiple decentralized trading venues or supporting new blockchain ecosystem launches.
  • Knowledge of emerging DeFi liquidity provisioning techniques, market structure innovations, and evolving liquidity incentive models.

Circle is on a mission to create an inclusive financial future, with transparency at our core. We consider a wide variety of elements when crafting our compensation ranges and total compensation packages.

Starting pay is determined by various factors, including but not limited to: relevant experience, skill set, qualifications, and other business and organizational needs. Please note that compensation ranges may differ for candidates in other locations.

We are an equal opportunity employer. Additionally, Circle participates in the E-Verify Program in certain locations, as required by law.

jobs.title: Security Engineer III/DLP
jobs.excerpt: By joining Sedgwick, you'll be part of something truly meaningful.
jobs.description:
By joining Sedgwick, you'll be part of something truly meaningful. It’s what our 33,000 colleagues do every day for people around the world who are facing the unexpected. We invite you to grow your career with us, experience our caring culture, and enjoy work-life balance. Here, there’s no limit to what you can achieve.

Newsweek Recognizes Sedgwick as America’s Greatest Workplaces National Top Companies

Certified as a Great Place to Work®

Fortune Best Workplaces in Financial Services & Insurance

Security Engineer III/DLP

.

Primary purpose


The Security Engineer is responsible for implementing, maintaining, monitoring, and managing secure solutions in accordance with the organization’s architectural designs, best practices, and regulatory or compliance requirements. As risks change, the engineer recommends modifications and enhancements so the organization keeps pace with the threat landscape, and contributes to the corporate security strategy alongside security leadership and senior technologists.


This role focuses on designing, implementing, and managing Data Loss Prevention (DLP) and Microsoft Purview solutions to protect sensitive organizational data. The engineer develops and enforces data protection policies, monitors data activity across endpoints, cloud services, and on-premises environments, and ensures compliance with regulatory and corporate requirements. The engineer also advances Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) capabilities by identifying data risks, improving data visibility, classifying sensitive information, and strengthening data governance and security controls.


The engineer’s work supports IT infrastructure, application development, security operations, security audit, and end users, with an emphasis on securing systems, applications, third-party connections, service providers, and business-to-business initiatives. The ideal candidate collaborates with cross-functional teams to continuously assess and improve the organization’s data security posture, respond to incidents, and align with evolving security standards and best practices.

Essential functions and responsibilities

Data protection and DSPM


  • Design, implement, and tune DLP and Microsoft Purview policies, including sensitivity labels, classification, and data protection controls across endpoints, cloud services, email, collaboration platforms, and on-premises repositories.
  • Monitor data activity, triage and investigate DLP alerts, and work with the SOC and incident responders on data exposure events.
  • Identify data risks, improve data visibility, and report on data security posture with measurable benchmarks.
  • Partner with data owners, Legal, Privacy, and Compliance to define classification schemes and handling requirements, and to support data governance.

Operations and delivery


  • Handle daily implementation, monitoring, and operational support of hardware, software, customer applications, managed solutions, and service provider relationships.
  • Deliver information security projects on time, within budget, and within SLAs, evaluating existing security infrastructure and proposing changes as directed by security leadership and architects.
  • Manage service and escalation tickets within SLA expectations.
  • Participate regularly in change and project management meetings, and work closely with project managers to meet milestones.
  • Develop security test plans from architectural designs, identify deficiencies, and make enhancements so production is not impacted.
  • Research, validate, and deploy solutions that meet security and business needs, following security engineering fundamentals and processes in NIST 800-160.

Incident response


  • Assist with incident response and system stability issues, which may include involvement outside regular work hours.
  • Influence the planning and execution of incident response and postmortem exercises, with measurable benchmarks that show progress or gaps.

Automation and improvement


  • Develop technical solutions and new security tools to mitigate vulnerabilities and automate repeatable tasks, enabling the team to focus on more advanced work.
  • Conduct performance testing to stress the limits of security solutions without harming business processes.
  • Lead IT groups and business units as needed in troubleshooting compatibility issues between security tools and business or productivity programs.

Communication and collaboration


  • Work with architects, the SOC, incident responders, and infrastructure and development teams.
  • Analyze client and customer needs and provide clear, concise reports to leadership.
  • Work with management on assigned projects from inception through implementation, maintaining internal communication and user involvement.
  • Provide feedback and suggestions to management to improve IT security processes and procedures.

Additional functions


  • Perform other duties as assigned.
  • Travel as required.

Qualifications

Education and licensing


  • Bachelor’s degree in management information systems or a related field, and be pursuing a master’s degree in business administration or an IT-related field. Licenses as needed.

Experience


  • Three or more years of experience in cybersecurity with a systems or network security engineering background.
  • Preferably 2+ years of additional IT experience in technology design, implementation, and delivery.
  • Hands-on experience with DLP and Microsoft Purview, including sensitivity labels, DLP policy design, and data classification.
  • Extensive knowledge of traditional and modern security controls, such as SIEM, IDS/IPS, PKI, IDAM, antivirus, firewalls, EDR, threat intelligence platforms, security automation and orchestration, deception technologies, and application controls.
  • Experience managing SIEM, threat intelligence, automation and orchestration, IDS/IPS, file integrity monitoring (FIM), DLP, and other monitoring tools.

Preferred experience


  • DSPM tools and practices.
  • Application control listing software, SIEM solutions, and XDR solutions.
  • Artificial intelligence and machine learning, including data security considerations for AI.
  • CIS hardening.
  • Researching and advising leadership on emerging security technologies.
  • One or more of ISO 27001, NIST, PCI DSS, HIPAA, HITECH, SOX, GDPR, CIS standards, or SOC 2.

Skills and knowledge


  • Ability to work independently and solve problems as they arise.
  • Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with integrity.
  • Ability to continuously learn new technologies and guide team collaboration.
  • CIA triad and IT security frameworks expertise.
  • CISSP preferred. CISM, SANS, Microsoft security certifications (such as SC-401), or other security-related certifications are a plus.

Work environment


  • When applicable and appropriate, reasonable accommodations will be considered.
  • Mental: clear, conceptual thinking, excellent judgment, troubleshooting, problem solving, analysis, and discretion; ability to handle stress, manage multiple priorities, and meet deadlines.
  • Physical: computer keyboarding; travel as required.
  • Auditory/visual: hearing, vision, and talking.

Sedgwick is an Equal Opportunity Employer and a Drug-Free Workplace.

If you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, consider applying for it anyway! Sedgwick is building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace and recognizes that each person possesses a unique combination of skills, knowledge, and experience. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.
